<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Original run/kernel binding prerequisite

This internal prerequisite records a controller-attributed child run's original
managed endpoint. It prepares for [D81](DECISIONS.md): children are runs in their
existing session, using its environment, workspace and grants, with kernels of
their own. It does not route a cell, start a child or kernel, or complete D81.

No worker HTTP route, WorkerClient method, tool, launcher, policy, approval,
profile loader or grant is added. `ExecutionContext`, existing MAIN kernels,
session observations, lineage keys and cancellation behavior are unchanged.
The draft delegation concurrency/depth and role defaults remain separate.

## Attribution and original identity

[`RunKernelScope`](../packages/contracts/src/sandbox_science/contracts/run_kernels.py)
contains the explicit project, session, environment, original parent run,
delegation and child run IDs. Parent and child must be distinct and cannot
impersonate USER. All identifiers are bounded ASCII. The future caller must
derive these values from its genuine admitted controller context and original
records. Construction and validation establish neither authentication nor that
admission. Actor, operation, execution or synthetic session IDs cannot stand in
for the child run.

`RunKernelBinding` adds a complete original managed sandbox name, immutable VM
ID and daemon incarnation. It is an endpoint enrollment observation, **not** a
kernel birth, start revision, loaded state, successful dispatch or run-start
proof. Enrollment after an earlier unseen start cannot establish that earlier
start. A future dispatcher must enroll before its first child effect and retain
the binding alongside the original accepted attempt.

The version-1 binding key hashes compact sorted ASCII JSON containing the complete
binding under `run-kernel-binding-v1` followed by NUL. Receipt time and operation
ID are excluded from that identity key. The separate canonical request digest
includes the original binding and operation ID under `run-kernel-enrollment-v1`
followed by NUL. All fields are validated before aggregate encoding; copied extra
fields and model/scalar subclasses are refused before their callbacks.

## Internal methods and proof

[`ExecutionManager.enroll_run_kernel(scope, operation_id, initialize=False)`](../packages/worker/src/sandbox_science/worker/manager.py)
is synchronous and internal. Its new method is not called by existing APIs.
It requires an already connected, unfenced, unlocked, nonclosed/nondetaching
channel and an explicitly configured trusted managed VM identity. The single
bounded retained endpoint row must have original TEXT identity fields matching
that exact channel incarnation and managed name/immutable ID. Unknown,
unmanaged, corrupt, missing or contradictory identity refuses.

The method performs no await, RPC, CLI, reconnect, wake, environment/kernel
creation, lifecycle lock acquisition or activity/busy-counter update. It
rechecks the exact environment/channel objects, incarnation, retained endpoint
and trusted managed identity before and after the enrollment transaction, and
after commit. A failure inside the transaction rolls back its record and first
schema creation. A postcommit failure returns unavailable while retaining the
original audit; it does not erase, re-enroll or repeat possible effects.

A readable CP-13 package hold does not prevent this metadata observation.
Enrollment grants no package admission exemption: a later dispatcher must apply
ordinary CP-13 and controller/session admission before actual launch. Receipt
time is a trusted host observation, not an atomic external VM-health or
filesystem snapshot and not an opaque session-open lifetime.

[`RunKernelBindings`](../packages/worker/src/sandbox_science/worker/run_kernels.py)
borrows the canonical worker `Store` connection and transaction seam. Its lower
level `enroll(binding, operation_id, initialize=False, validate=None)` stores
explicit trusted attribution. It cannot authenticate endpoints by itself;
the manager supplies its synchronous fresh-proof callback. `get(scope)` reads
one exact historical scoped receipt without requiring or inventing a current
endpoint. Historical reads confer no eligibility to use that VM or a kernel.

## Durability, replay and bounds

One immutable row contains the complete binding, required explicit format
version, operation/request digest, binding key and trusted UTC receipt time.
The original child cannot change session, environment, parent, delegation, VM
or incarnation. A delegation or parent-scoped operation cannot alias another
child. A different project's scoped read sees no record. Exact replay returns
the original receipt unchanged, including its time; changed requests conflict.
Worker reconnect on the same original managed incarnation may replay the
existing binding. A newer incarnation or replacement VM cannot backfill it.

Namespace creation occurs only during explicitly requested first enrollment,
inside the same transaction as its record. Ordinary Store startup and legacy
execution paths neither initialize nor read it. Missing default namespace is
not found; partial/unsupported schemas and corrupt records refuse. Complete
erasure of every namespace table cannot be distinguished from prior absence
without an external retained initialization proof. `initialize=True` is not
that proof and must not become automatic lost-history recovery.

| Engineering bound | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Identifier | 128 ASCII characters |
| Canonical receipt | 4 KiB |
| Retained bindings | 256/project; 1,024/global |
| Logical retained bytes | 2 MiB/project; 8 MiB/global |
| Historical read | One selected bounded row |

Every stored variable column, full receipt and fixed row reservation contributes
to transactional accounting; one fixed metadata reservation counts globally.
Count ceilings are checked before the bounded aggregate pass, and scalar byte
charges are type/range guarded before summation. A full quota or invalid charge
refuses a new binding. There is no eviction, overwrite, rebinding or ID reuse.
These logical limits do not measure SQLite page/index allocation, RSS or
arbitrary external database growth. Immutable triggers and canonical coherence
checks do not authenticate against an administrator rewriting all database state.

Selected SQL type/byte projections precede Python parsing. Empty/wrong-type or
overlong endpoint and receipt fields cannot normalize into known provenance.
Retained duplicate JSON keys, mismatched columns/request/key/charge and malformed
versions refuse. Damage to this unwired namespace does not enter ordinary
legacy Store startup, execution or kernel generation reads.

The component owns no thread, async task, connection or close method. The
existing synchronous Store transaction owns admitted work. A future async
adapter must serialize use of the borrowed connection and retain/drain actual
queue, SQL and file ownership through timeout, repeated cancellation and
shutdown. Cancelling a future is not proof that SQL stopped. No new async
ownership or cross-request session-lifetime guarantee is implemented here.

## Complete internal dispatcher that remains next

The next increment must move all run-aware paths together, rather than adding
only a caller `run_id` or changing the executor dictionary key:

1. A trusted admitted controller supplies the original child scope and enrollment
   before dispatch; fresh session-open/project/grant checks remain caller-owned.
   Legacy MAIN requests retain their existing namespace. No model parameter can
   manufacture controller authority or reuse another child's binding.
2. Negotiate a distinct executor run-kernel protocol and refuse legacy peers
   before accepting child work. Carry the exact original enrollment/attempt and
   VM/incarnation through recovery; unknown admission or effect is reconciled,
   never silently repeated or attached to today's endpoint.
3. Route a child to a `(project, session, child run, language)` interpreter using
   the existing session workspace/environment. Use separate bounded run
   generation/birth records, preserving raw and normalized generation and exact
   original birth/start revision. Sharing workspace and uid establishes no new
   filesystem or security isolation between children.
4. Bind cell state/result, restart and child-only close/cancel to that exact run
   and original incarnation. Existing execution-ID cancellation stays exact;
   parent/sibling kernels survive child cancellation or restart. Session close
   still stops every run. CP-13 launch gates and kernel-start transactions remain
   mandatory, including cancellation while queued or starting.
5. Add a separate bounded run-aware status/lineage projection and passive
   no-wake checks. Preserve the <=2-language legacy MAIN GUI/notice response and
   keys until an explicit consumer increment is reviewed. No provisional birth,
   current-package inference, activity refresh or state-lost consumption occurs
   during passive reads.

Focused tests use disposable local Store databases and constructed channels
that never start. They cover original identity, immutable replay, wrong scopes,
strict copied inputs, quota/transaction rollback, real commit followed by lost
acknowledgment, concurrent first enrollment, bounded corrupt reads, same-original
incarnation replay and changed/unknown managed proof. No service, model, RPC,
research kernel, VM or browser is started by this prerequisite's author. Root
integration, independent review, combined gates and later real OpenShell D81
acceptance remain separate.

Author validation on Python 3.13: 217 affected tests pass, including all 44 new
record/fake-channel cases and the existing contract suite. Whole contracts/worker
source plus the new tests type-check with zero errors/warnings. Full-repository
Ruff and format, locked dependency sync, 75 installed license checks and protocol
generation checks pass. Initial style/type diagnostics remain retained separately;
the initial 38 focused cases and later 43-case run were successful predecessor
runs, not substitutes for the final affected output. No full-repository Python
suite or real kernel/VM acceptance is claimed here.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Internal original run/kernel enrollment observations, without execution grants."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Annotated, Literal, Self, cast

from pydantic import ConfigDict, Field, field_validator, model_validator

from .model import Contract, Identifier

MAX_RUN_KERNEL_RECORD = 4096
_SCOPE_FIELDS = (
    "project_id",
    "session_id",
    "environment_id",
    "parent_run_id",
    "delegation_id",
    "child_run_id",
)


class RunKernelScope(Contract):
    """Explicit trusted controller attribution, never authentication or a grant.

    The caller must supply the genuine recorded parent/delegation/child identity.
    No actor, execution or synthetic session can substitute for that identity.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, strict=True)
    project_id: Identifier
    session_id: Identifier
    environment_id: Identifier
    parent_run_id: Identifier
    delegation_id: Identifier
    child_run_id: Identifier

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _runs(self) -> Self:
        if (
            self.parent_run_id.casefold() == "user"
            or self.child_run_id.casefold() == "user"
            or self.parent_run_id == self.child_run_id
        ):
            raise ValueError("a child requires distinct original non-USER run identities")
        return self


class RunKernelBinding(Contract):
    """Original managed endpoint observation; no kernel birth or revision claim."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, strict=True)
    scope: RunKernelScope
    sandbox: Identifier
    sandbox_id: Identifier
    incarnation: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^inc-[0-9a-f]{24}$")]


class RunKernelEnrollment(Contract):
    """One immutable historical receipt, not dispatch or current eligibility."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, strict=True)
    format_version: Literal[1]
    operation_id: Identifier
    request_sha256: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")]
    binding_sha256: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")]
    binding: RunKernelBinding
    recorded_at: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=40)]

    @field_validator("format_version", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _version(cls, value: object) -> object:
        if type(value) is not int:
            raise ValueError("enrollment version must be an exact integer")
        return value

    @field_validator("recorded_at")
    @classmethod
    def _utc(cls, value: str) -> str:
        stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
        offset = stamp.utcoffset()
        if offset is None or offset.total_seconds() != 0:
            raise ValueError("enrollment receipt time needs a UTC offset")
        return value


def _fields(value: object, model: type[Contract]) -> dict[str, object]:
    if type(value) is not model:
        raise ValueError("invalid run/kernel model type")
    fields = object.__getattribute__(value, "__dict__")
    extras = object.__getattribute__(value, "__pydantic_extra__")
    if type(fields) is not dict or extras is not None:
        raise ValueError("undeclared run/kernel model fields")
    declared = cast(dict[object, object], fields)
    if (
        len(declared) != len(model.model_fields)
        or any(type(key) is not str for key in declared)
        or set(declared) != set(model.model_fields)
    ):
        raise ValueError("undeclared run/kernel model fields")
    return cast(dict[str, object], declared)


def _text(value: object) -> str:
    if type(value) is not str or not 1 <= len(value) <= 128 or not value.isascii():
        raise ValueError("invalid run/kernel scalar")
    return value


def checked_run_kernel_scope(value: RunKernelScope) -> RunKernelScope:
    """Copy and strictly validate bounded built-in fields before aggregate encoding."""
    fields = _fields(value, RunKernelScope)
    return RunKernelScope.model_validate(
        {name: _text(fields[name]) for name in _SCOPE_FIELDS}, strict=True
    )


def checked_run_kernel_binding(value: RunKernelBinding) -> RunKernelBinding:
    """Reject copied extras/subtypes and unknown original VM/incarnation fields."""
    fields = _fields(value, RunKernelBinding)
    scope = checked_run_kernel_scope(cast(RunKernelScope, fields["scope"]))
    return RunKernelBinding(
        scope=scope,
        sandbox=_text(fields["sandbox"]),
        sandbox_id=_text(fields["sandbox_id"]),
        incarnation=_text(fields["incarnation"]),
    )


def run_kernel_binding_sha256(value: RunKernelBinding) -> str:
    """Canonical v1 original identity key; neither current state nor grants enter it."""
    binding = checked_run_kernel_binding(value)
    raw = json.dumps(
        binding.model_dump(mode="json"), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True
    ).encode("ascii")
    return hashlib.sha256(b"run-kernel-binding-v1\0" + raw).hexdigest()

"""Executions: submission, dispatch to executors, events, cancellation and files.

docs/specs/tools.md defines the behavior. Every execution is persisted before
it is dispatched, and every event before it is delivered, so a client can
reconnect and replay. A restarted worker reconciles daemon attempts and reports
unrecoverable attempts as ``lost`` instead of running them again. What an executor
sends is untrusted: it is checked and bounded before it changes any state, and every execution
reaches a terminal state whatever the executor does.
"""

SHARED_TIMEOUT = 120.0
"""The longest one step of the shared files' sync may take around a call (D79)."""
MAX_HELD_NOTICES = 20
"""Sync notices held for one call's or one session's next result."""
MAX_HELD_BYTES = 16 * 1024
MAX_HELD_SESSIONS = 256
_UNSYNCED = (
    "shared/ could not be synced with the project's other environments just now; "
    "it is synced again at the next call"
)
WATCHDOG_GRACE = 30.0
"""Seconds past an execution's own limit before the worker cancels it itself."""
CANCEL_GRACE = 30.0
"""Seconds to confirm job cancellation before abandoning its executor connection."""
LOST_GRACE = 60.0
"""Seconds after that cancel before the worker gives the attempt up as lost."""
RETAIN_LIVE = 600.0
"""Seconds a finished execution stays in memory for clients still streaming it."""
EVENT_PAGE = 64
"""Events read from the store at a time when a client replays a stream."""
OUTPUT_BUDGET = 4
"""Stream text and rich output an execution may store as events, in multiples of its
output limit (UTF-8 bytes). An honest executor stays under three: half the limit of each
stream, which can triple when invalid bytes become U+FFFD, plus the limit of outputs."""
MAX_EVENTS = 100_000
"""Stream and output events stored for one execution; later ones are dropped."""
MAX_ERROR_TEXT = 64 * 1024
MAX_TRACEBACK_LINES = 100
MAX_TRACEBACK_LINE = 8 * 1024
MAX_WRITTEN = 1000
MAX_LIST = 5000
MAX_HOSTNAME = 255
MAX_REVISIONS = 64
"""``revision`` events one execution may report; later ones are dropped."""
MAX_EXECUTION_LOCKFILES = 4
"""Lockfiles one execution's ``revision`` events may bring or have asked for: one for each
attempt whose package commands made a change. A revision left without one gets the
current lockfile asked for instead, while it is current."""
LOCKFILE_TIMEOUT = 120.0
"""Seconds the executor gets to send the current revision's lockfile."""
_EXECUTION = re.compile(r"exe-[0-9a-f]{24}")


class _DaemonIncarnationError(WorkerError):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "the sandbox executor incarnation was lost")


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


def _integer(value: object, low: int = -(2**31), high: int = 2**31 - 1) -> int | None:
    if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and low <= value <= high:
        return value
    return None


def _epoch(value: object) -> datetime | None:
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool):
        with contextlib.suppress(OverflowError, OSError, ValueError):
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(value, UTC)
    return None


def _seconds(value: object) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool) and math.isfinite(value):
        return max(0.0, float(value))
    return 0.0


def _text(value: object, limit: int) -> str | None:
    """A string from the executor, keeping its head and tail if it is over ``limit``."""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None
    if len(value) <= limit:
        return value
    half = limit // 2
    return f"{value[:half]}\n[… {len(value) - 2 * half} characters omitted …]\n{value[-half:]}"


@dataclass
class _Live:
    execution: Execution
    environment_id: str
    changed: asyncio.Future[None]
    final_source_seq: int | None = None
    observation: OutputReport | None = None
    observation_gap: Gap | None = "missing"
    limit: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT
    cancel_requested: bool = False
    dispatched: bool = False
    reattached: bool = False
    """An unseen kernel birth replayed after detach cannot establish a new start pin."""
    watchdog: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
    cancel_watchdog: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
    stored: int = 0
    """Bytes of stream text and rich output stored as events."""
    events: int = 0
    overflowed: bool = False
    channel: ExecutorChannel | None = None
    """The executor the execution was sent to: only it may cancel or lose it."""
    notices: list[str] = field(default_factory=list[str])
    """What syncing the project's shared files told before the execution ran (D79)."""
    dispatched_at: float = 0.0
    """When the request went to the executor, by the monotonic clock."""
    final: tuple[ExecutionState, Result] | None = None
    """The executor's outcome, held while the shared files sync after it (D79)."""
    ended_at: float = 0.0
    """When the executor reported the outcome, by the monotonic clock."""
    revisions: int = 0
    """``revision`` events it carried."""
    lockfiles: int = 0
    """Lockfiles its ``revision`` events brought or had asked for."""
    lockfile_attempts: set[str] = field(default_factory=set[str])
    """The attempts whose lockfiles its ``revision`` events brought."""


@dataclass
class _Environment:
    lock: asyncio.Lock = field(default_factory=asyncio.Lock)
    channel: ExecutorChannel | None = None
    location: Location | None = None
    languages: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    features: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    running: set[str] = field(default_factory=set[str])
    last_used: float = field(default_factory=time.monotonic)
    """Last ordinary use, by the monotonic clock; passive observers never refresh it."""
    requests: int = 0
    """Ordinary requests in flight: files, publication and explicit kernel operations."""


@dataclass
class _KernelObserver:
    scope: tuple[str, str, str]
    valid: bool = True
    """A matching session close invalidates only this active, bounded observation."""


KERNEL_OBSERVATION_TIMEOUT = 2.0
"""Whole existing-channel RPC budget, including the transport write lock."""
MAX_KERNEL_OBSERVATIONS = 8
"""No queued observers, and at most one in flight for each environment."""


_Observation = TypeVar("_Observation")

Notices = Callable[[str, datetime], list[tuple[datetime, str]]]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Activity:
    """What an environment is doing, as the worker sees it, for idle suspension (W3)."""

    last_used: float | None
    """When the worker last asked anything of it (monotonic clock); None if never since it

    running: int
    cpu_seconds: float | None
    """CPU time used below its executor so far; None without an executor, when no research
    code runs there."""
    kernels: int
    executor: str | None = None
    """The executor's incarnation, so that CPU samples of different executors are not

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Range:

    size: int
    sha256: str | None
    modified: datetime | None
    offset: int
    data: bytes
    content_b64: str
    eof: bool
    stamp: str | None = None


@dataclass
class _Publication:
    lease: CaptureLease
    certain: bool = True


class ExecutionManager:
    def __init__(
        self,
        store: Store,
        backend: Backend,
        blobs: Blobs,
        *,
        pool_id: str,
        max_artifact_size: int,
        state_dir: Path,
        shared: SharedSync | None = None,
        package_cache: str | None = None,
        capture_timeout: float = 30.0,
    ) -> None:
        if (
            isinstance(capture_timeout, bool)
            or not math.isfinite(capture_timeout)
            or not 0.05 <= capture_timeout <= 60
        ):
            raise ValueError("capture_timeout must be between 0.05 and 60 seconds")
        self.store = store
        self.backend = backend
        self.blobs = blobs
        self.shared = shared
        """Keeps the project's shared files in step across its environments (D79)."""
        self.revisions = Revisions(store, Blobs(state_dir / "lockfiles"), cache=package_cache)
        """Each environment's revisions, with their lockfiles (Conda provisioning, W3).
        ``package_cache`` is the cache's URL as sandboxes reach it, which lockfiles never
        name."""
        self._lockfile_locks: dict[str, asyncio.Lock] = {}
        """One lockfile at a time is checked for each environment, in a thread."""
        self._fetching: set[str] = set()
        """Environments whose executor is asked for the current lockfile."""
        self.pool_id = pool_id
        self.max_artifact_size = max_artifact_size
        self.capture_timeout = capture_timeout
        self._captures: set[asyncio.Task[ArtifactRef]] = set()
        self._capture_owners: dict[asyncio.Task[ArtifactRef], _Publication] = {}
        self._capture_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        self._blob_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4, thread_name_prefix="artifact-blob")
        self._closing_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        # The isolation probe's sentinel goes here, among the worker's own files.
        self.state_dir = state_dir
        self._live: dict[str, _Live] = {}
        self._held_notices: OrderedDict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = OrderedDict()
        """Notices from syncing shared files for file requests, by environment and session,
        for the session's next result there (D79)."""
        self._environments: dict[str, _Environment] = {}
        self._channels: set[ExecutorChannel] = set()
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task[Any]] = set()
        self._closing = False
        self._recovering: set[str] = set()
        self._pollers: dict[str, tuple[ExecutorChannel, asyncio.Task[Any]]] = {}
        self._daemon_fences: dict[str, asyncio.Task[None]] = {}
        self._quarantined: set[str] = set()
        self.job_resources: Callable[[str], Resources] | None = None
        self.confirmed_daemon_loss: Callable[[str], Awaitable[bool]] | None = None
        self.daemon_identity: Callable[[str], tuple[str, str] | None] | None = None
        self.recycle_daemon: Callable[[str, str, str], Awaitable[None]] | None = None
        self._closing_sessions: dict[tuple[str, str, str], int] = {}
        self._released_environments: dict[str, int] = {}
        self._kernel_observations: dict[str, _KernelObserver] = {}
        self.notices: Notices | None = None
        """Admission notices for an environment since a time; the environments set it."""
        self._noticed: dict[tuple[str, str], datetime] = {}
        self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()
        self._gate_locks: dict[str, asyncio.Lock] = {}
        self._gate_acked: dict[ExecutorChannel, PackageGate] = {}
        self._gate_retries: dict[str, asyncio.Task[Any]] = {}

    def package_admission(self, environment_id: str) -> PackageGate:
        gate = self.store.package_gate(environment_id)
        if gate.mode == "needs_recovery":
            raise recovery_refusal(gate)
        return gate

    def _package_origin(self, request: ExecutionRequest, origin: str | None) -> None:
        if origin is None:
            self.package_admission(request.context.environment_id)
            return
        saved = self.store.provision_authority(origin)
        if (
            not isinstance(request, ShellRequest)
            or saved is None
            or saved[0] != request.context
            or saved[1] is ProvisionState.FINISHED
            or self.store.provision_step(origin, request.operation_id)
            != hashlib.sha256(request.model_dump_json().encode()).hexdigest()
            or not request.operation_id.startswith(origin + ".")
            or re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,95}", request.operation_id[len(origin) + 1 :])
            is None
        ):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "invalid internal provisioning operation")
        gate = self.package_admission(request.context.environment_id)
        if gate.mode == "hold" and gate.operation != origin:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "another provisioning operation holds admission"
            )

    async def _sync_package_gate(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> bool:
        identity = channel.hello.get("package_gate")
        if not isinstance(identity, str) or re.fullmatch(r"gate-[0-9a-f]{24}", identity) is None:
            return False
        lock = self._gate_locks.setdefault(environment_id, asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            binding = self.daemon_identity(environment_id) if self.daemon_identity else None
            try:
                self.store.bind_package_gate(
                    environment_id,
                    repr(
                        binding
                        or (
                            self.backend.name,
                            str(getattr(self.backend, "root", "")),
                            self.backend.sandbox_id(environment_id),
                        )
                    ),
                )
            except WorkerError:
                return False  # no gate mutation on an unproven or replacement sandbox
            while True:
                gate = self.store.package_gate(environment_id)
                if self._gate_acked.get(channel) == gate:
                    return True
                reply = await channel.request(
                    "package_gate",
                    incarnation=identity,
                    generation=gate.generation,
                    mode=gate.mode,
                    operation=gate.operation,
                    revision=gate.revision,
                )
                if channel.closed or (
                    self.daemon_identity is not None
                    and self.daemon_identity(environment_id) != binding
                ):
                    raise WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "package admission binding changed during ACK"
                    )
                if reply.get("incarnation") != identity or any(
                    reply.get(key) != value or type(reply.get(key)) is not type(value)
                    for key, value in gate.fields().items()
                ):
                    raise WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "invalid package admission acknowledgement"
                    )
                self._gate_acked[channel] = gate
                if gate == self.store.package_gate(environment_id):
                    return True

    async def sync_package_gate(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        environment = await self._environment(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel
        if channel is None or not await self._sync_package_gate(environment_id, channel):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "legacy executor lacks package admission fencing; protected work refused",
            )

    def refresh_package_gate(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Bounded retry of release/classification ACK; uncertainty leaves the guest closed."""
        if self._closing or environment_id in self._gate_retries:
            return

        async def retry() -> None:
            try:
                for delay in (0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2):
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                    try:
                        await self.sync_package_gate(environment_id)
                        return
                    except WorkerError:
                        pass
            finally:
                self._gate_retries.pop(environment_id, None)

        self._gate_retries[environment_id] = self._spawn(retry())

    async def start(self) -> None:
        """Recover known daemon executions without ever resubmitting a command."""
        daemon_enabled = getattr(getattr(self.backend, "settings", None), "daemon", False)
        endpoints = tuple(set(self.store.endpoints()) | set(self.store.pending_recycles()))
        if endpoints and not daemon_enabled:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "sandbox daemon endpoints remain; explicitly release or recycle their "
                "sandboxes before disabling daemon transport; startup refused",
            )
        recovery: dict[str, list[_Live]] = {key: [] for key in endpoints}
        for execution_id, execution in self.store.unfinished():
            if execution is None:
                self.store.mark_terminal(execution_id)
                continue
            last = max(execution.last_seq, self.store.last_seq(execution_id))
            saved = self.store.recovery(execution_id)
            try:
                request = _REQUEST.validate_json(saved[0]) if saved is not None else None
            except ValueError:
                request = None
                saved = None
            live = self._track(
                execution.model_copy(update={"last_seq": last}),
                request.output_limit_bytes if request else DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT,
            )
            live.events, live.stored = self.store.event_usage(execution_id)
            if saved is not None and saved[1] and daemon_enabled:
                live.dispatched = True
                live.cancel_requested = saved[3] or execution.origin is not None
                recovery.setdefault(execution.context.environment_id, []).append(live)
            else:
                self._lose(live, "the worker that restarted without a recoverable daemon dispatch")
        for environment_id, lives in recovery.items():
            await self._recover(environment_id, lives, startup=True)

    async def _recover(
        self, environment_id: str, lives: list[_Live], *, startup: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        if environment_id in self._recovering or self._closing:
            return
        self._recovering.add(environment_id)
        retry = False
        try:
            # Keep an existing watchdog across reconnects. At startup reconstruct one
            # absolute deadline, including its original grace, rather than refreshing it.
            for live in lives:
                live.reattached = True
                if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
                    continue
                saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
                if saved is not None and (live.watchdog is None or live.watchdog.done()):
                    request = _REQUEST.validate_json(saved[0])
                    elapsed = max(
                        0.0,
                        (
                            _now() - (live.execution.started_at or live.execution.submitted_at)
                        ).total_seconds(),
                    )
                    live.watchdog = self._spawn(
                        self._watch(live, request.timeout_seconds - elapsed)
                    )
            if self.confirmed_daemon_loss is not None and await self.confirmed_daemon_loss(
                environment_id
            ):
                self.store.forget_endpoint(environment_id)
                self._quarantined.discard(environment_id)
                for live in lives:
                    self._lose(live, "the sandbox that was deleted, stopped or replaced")
                return
            channel: ExecutorChannel | None = None
            for attempt in range(5):
                try:
                    environment = await self._environment(environment_id)
                    channel = environment.channel
                    if channel is not None:
                        break
                except WorkerError:
                    if self.confirmed_daemon_loss is not None and await self.confirmed_daemon_loss(
                        environment_id
                    ):
                        self.store.forget_endpoint(environment_id)
                        self._quarantined.discard(environment_id)
                        for live in lives:
                            self._lose(live, "the sandbox that was deleted, stopped or replaced")
                        return
                    if attempt == 4:
                        break
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.2 * (attempt + 1))
            if channel is None:
                if startup:
                    raise WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                        "cannot reconcile the sandbox daemon; startup refused",
                    )
                retry = True
                return
            try:
                await self._reconcile_unknown(channel)
            except WorkerError as exc:
                await channel.shutdown()
                if startup:
                    raise WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                        "cannot quiesce unknown daemon tasks; startup refused",
                    ) from exc
                channel = None
            for live in lives:
                if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
                    continue
                saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
                if channel is None or saved is None or channel.incarnation != saved[1]:
                    self._lose(live, "the sandbox executor incarnation")
                    continue
                live.channel = channel
                live.dispatched = True
                environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
                if environment is not None:
                    environment.running.add(live.execution.execution_id)
                if live.cancel_requested:
                    self.store.cancel_intent(live.execution.execution_id)
                    if live.cancel_watchdog is None or live.cancel_watchdog.done():
                        live.cancel_watchdog = self._spawn(self._watch_cancel(live))
                    try:
                        async with asyncio.timeout(CANCEL_GRACE):
                            await self._send_cancel(live)
                            if live.execution.origin is not None:
                                # Withdrawn provisioning ownership cannot leave an
                                # installer running while the service starts accepting work.
                                while live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                                    await self._replay(live, channel)
                                    if live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                                        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
                    except (WorkerError, TimeoutError):
                        await channel.shutdown()
                        self._lose(live, "the executor that did not confirm recovery cancellation")
                        continue
                try:
                    await self._replay(live, channel)
                except WorkerError:
                    await channel.close()
                    break
            if channel is not None:
                self._poll(environment_id, channel)
        finally:
            self._recovering.discard(environment_id)
            remaining = [
                live
                for live in lives
                if live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
                and live.channel is not None
                and live.channel.closed
            ]
            if (remaining or retry) and not self._closing:
                self._spawn(self._retry_recovery(environment_id, lives))

    async def _retry_recovery(self, environment_id: str, lives: list[_Live]) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
        await self._recover(environment_id, lives)

    async def _reconcile_unknown(self, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        """Withdraw control-created tasks whose ownership did not survive the worker.

        Reconciliation can only cancel IDs; no sandbox claim can create work or widen
        the saved limits of a known attempt.
        """
        known = {
            key for key, live in self._live.items() if live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
        }
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(CANCEL_GRACE):
                reply = await channel.request("active")
                raw: Any = reply.get("executions")
                if (
                    not isinstance(raw, list)
                    or len(cast(list[object], raw)) > 128
                    or any(
                        not isinstance(key, str) or re.fullmatch(r"exe-[0-9a-f]{24}", key) is None
                        for key in cast(list[object], raw)
                    )
                ):
                    raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "invalid executor reconciliation")
                unknown = set(cast(list[str], raw)) - known
                for key in unknown:
                    await channel.request("cancel", execution=key)
                while unknown:
                    reply = await channel.request("active")
                    raw = reply.get("executions")
                    if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(cast(list[object], raw)) > 128:
                        raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "invalid executor reconciliation")
                    unknown.intersection_update(
                        item for item in cast(list[object], raw) if isinstance(item, str)
                    )
                    if unknown:
                        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "unknown executor tasks did not stop") from exc

    def _poll(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        previous = self._pollers.get(environment_id)
        if previous is not None and not previous[1].done():
            if previous[0] is channel:
                return
            previous[1].cancel()
        self._pollers[environment_id] = (
            channel,
            self._spawn(self._poll_daemon(environment_id, channel)),
        )

    async def _replay(self, live: _Live, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
        reply = await channel.request(
            "replay",
            execution=live.execution.execution_id,
            after=saved[2] if saved else 0,
            reply_timeout=30,
        )
        if reply.get("found") is not True and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
            self._lose(live, "the executor with no retained execution record")

    async def _poll_daemon(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        while not self._closing and not channel.closed:
            try:
                for live in list(self._live.values()):
                    if (
                        live.channel is channel
                        and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
                        and live.final is None
                    ):
                        await self._replay(live, channel)
            except WorkerError:
                await channel.close()
                return
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

    async def release(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Stop an environment's executor before its sandbox goes away.

        Attempts still running there end as the executor's channel closes.
        """
        await self.guard_package_deletion(environment_id)
        self._released_environments[environment_id] = (
            self._released_environments.get(environment_id, 0) + 1
        )
        try:
            await self._release(environment_id)
        finally:
            if self._released_environments[environment_id] == 1:
                self._released_environments.pop(environment_id)
            else:
                self._released_environments[environment_id] -= 1

    async def _release(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        captures = [
            task
            for task, owner in self._capture_owners.items()
            if owner.lease.environment_id == environment_id
        ]
        for task in captures:
            task.cancel()
        # VM cleanup cannot substitute for actual host blob/FD ownership. Keep
        # release pending through repeated cancellation until these tasks drain.
        _, cancelled = await capture.owned(asyncio.gather(*captures, return_exceptions=True))
        if cancelled:
            raise asyncio.CancelledError
        jobs = self._running_jobs(environment_id)
        await self._cancel_jobs(jobs)
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        if environment is None:
            return
        async with environment.lock:
            await self._drop(environment_id, environment)

    async def _drop(self, environment_id: str, environment: _Environment) -> None:
        """Forget an environment's record, then close its executor. Hold its lock.

        The record goes first, so that a request arriving meanwhile starts with a
        new one instead of opening an executor nobody tracks.
        """
        if self._environments.get(environment_id) is environment:
            self._environments.pop(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel
        if channel is not None:
            self._channels.discard(channel)
            await channel.shutdown()
            if not self.store.recycle_needed(environment_id):
                self.store.forget_endpoint(environment_id)

    async def activity(self, environment_id: str) -> Activity | None:
        """What an environment is doing now; None when its executor cannot say."""
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        if environment is None:
            return Activity(
                last_used=None,
                running=len(self._running_jobs(environment_id)),
                cpu_seconds=None,
                kernels=0,
            )
        busy = len(environment.running) + environment.requests
        busy += sum(
            1
            for job in self._running_jobs(environment_id)
            if job.execution_id not in environment.running
        )
        channel = environment.channel
        if channel is None or channel.closed:
            return Activity(environment.last_used, busy, None, 0)
        try:
            reply = await channel.request("usage", reply_timeout=10)
        except WorkerError:
            return None
        raw, kernels = reply.get("cpu_seconds"), reply.get("kernels")
        if (
            isinstance(raw, bool)
            or not isinstance(raw, int | float)
            or not isinstance(kernels, int)
        ):
            return None
        try:
            cpu = float(raw)  # an executor research code took over may send 10**400
        except OverflowError:
            return None
        if not math.isfinite(cpu) or cpu < 0:
            return None
        return Activity(environment.last_used, busy, cpu, kernels, channel.incarnation)

    async def release_if_idle(self, environment_id: str, idle_since: float) -> bool:
        """Stop an environment's executor if nothing ran in it or used it since ``idle_since``.

        Returns whether it did (or there was none), so that its sandbox may stop.
        """
        if self._running_jobs(environment_id) or any(
            owner.lease.environment_id == environment_id for owner in self._capture_owners.values()
        ):
            return False
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        if environment is None:
            return True
        async with environment.lock:
            if environment.running or environment.requests or environment.last_used > idle_since:
                return False
            await self._drop(environment_id, environment)
        return True

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Detach daemon bridges; stop stdio executors and report their attempts lost."""
        self._closing = True
        if self._closing_task is None:
            self._closing_task = asyncio.create_task(self._close())
        _, cancelled = await capture.owned(self._closing_task)
        if cancelled:
            raise asyncio.CancelledError

    async def _close(self) -> None:
        captures = list(self._captures)
        for task in captures:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*captures, return_exceptions=True)
        # Admitted blob work has drained before the pool/FDs or channels can close.
        self._blob_pool.shutdown(wait=True)
        tasks = list(self._tasks)
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        await asyncio.gather(
            *(
                channel.detach() if channel.daemon_token else channel.close()
                for channel in self._channels
            )
        )
        for live in list(self._live.values()):
            saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
            recoverable = (
                getattr(getattr(self.backend, "settings", None), "daemon", False)
                and live.dispatched
                and saved is not None
                and bool(saved[1])
            )
            if live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES and not recoverable:
                self._lose(live, "the worker")

    def _lose(self, live: _Live, what: str) -> None:
        """End an attempt whose outcome is unknown, because ``what`` stopped during it."""
        message = f"{what} stopped during this attempt; its outcome is unknown"
        if live.execution.job is not None:
            message += (
                "; partial whole logs remain at "
                + live.execution.job.stdout_path
                + " and "
                + live.execution.job.stderr_path
            )
        try:
            if live.final is not None:
                # The outcome is known; only the shared files' sync after it was cut short.
                self._complete(live, [*live.notices, _UNSYNCED])
                return
            self._finish(
                live,
                ExecutionState.LOST,
                Result(error=ErrorInfo(kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL, message=message)),
            )
        except Exception:
            _log.exception("could not report execution %s as lost", live.execution.execution_id)

    # Bookkeeping.

    def _spawn(self, coroutine: Any) -> asyncio.Task[Any]:
        task = asyncio.ensure_future(coroutine)
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)
        return task

    def _track(self, execution: Execution, limit: int = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_LIMIT) -> _Live:
        live = _Live(
            execution,
            execution.context.environment_id,
            asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future(),
            limit=limit,
        )
        self._live[execution.execution_id] = live
        return live

    def _save(self, live: _Live, **changes: Any) -> None:
        live.execution = live.execution.model_copy(update=changes)
        self.store.update_execution(live.execution)

    def _changed(self, live: _Live) -> None:
        changed, live.changed = live.changed, asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        changed.set_result(None)

    def _emit(self, live: _Live, make: Callable[[int, datetime], Event]) -> None:
        seq = live.execution.last_seq + 1
        event = make(seq, _now())
        live.execution = live.execution.model_copy(update={"last_seq": seq})
        source = _SOURCE_EVENT.get()
        acknowledged = (
            source[1] if source is not None and source[0] == live.execution.execution_id else None
        )
        self.store.commit_event(live.execution, event, acknowledged)
        self._changed(live)

    def _state(self, live: _Live, state: ExecutionState) -> None:
        execution_id = live.execution.execution_id
        self._emit(
            live,
            lambda seq, time: StateEvent(
                execution_id=execution_id, seq=seq, time=time, state=state
            ),
        )

    def _finish(self, live: _Live, state: ExecutionState, result: Result) -> None:
        """End an execution: its state event, result event and record are stored together."""
        if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
            return
        execution_id = live.execution.execution_id
        final, events = self._final(live.execution, state, result)
        source = _SOURCE_EVENT.get()
        acknowledged = live.final_source_seq
        if acknowledged is None and source is not None and source[0] == execution_id:
            acknowledged = source[1]
        self.store.finish(
            final,
            events,
            acknowledged,
            observation=live.observation,
            observation_gap=live.observation_gap,
        )
        live.execution = final
        self._changed(live)
        environment = self._environments.get(live.environment_id)
        if environment is not None:
            environment.running.discard(execution_id)
            environment.last_used = time.monotonic()
        if live.watchdog is not None and live.watchdog is not asyncio.current_task():
            live.watchdog.cancel()
        if live.cancel_watchdog is not None and live.cancel_watchdog is not asyncio.current_task():
            live.cancel_watchdog.cancel()
        asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(RETAIN_LIVE, self._live.pop, execution_id, None)

    def _final(
        self, execution: Execution, state: ExecutionState, result: Result
    ) -> tuple[Execution, tuple[StateEvent, ResultEvent]]:
        """The terminal record and its last two events, checked before anything is stored.

        Every value must survive a round trip through JSON and fit in one event
        line; a result that does not is shrunk, and failing that replaced.
        """
        unstorable = Result(
            error=ErrorInfo(
                kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL, message="the attempt's result could not be stored"
            )
        )
        candidates = (
            (state, result),
            (state, _shrunk(result)),
            (ExecutionState.FAILED, unstorable),
        )
        now = _now()
        seq = execution.last_seq
        for final_state, candidate in candidates:
            final = execution.model_copy(
                update={
                    "state": final_state,
                    "ended_at": now,
                    "result": candidate,
                    "last_seq": seq + 2,
                }
            )
            try:
                event = ResultEvent(
                    execution_id=execution.execution_id, seq=seq + 2, time=now, execution=final
                )
                encoded = _EVENT.dump_json(event)
                if len(encoded) > MAX_EVENT_BYTES:
                    raise ValueError(f"{len(encoded)} bytes")
                checked = _EVENT.validate_json(encoded)
            except ValueError as exc:  # PydanticSerializationError and ValidationError too
                _log.warning(
                    "execution %s: result not storable as reported (%s)",
                    execution.execution_id,
                    str(exc)[:300],
                )
                continue
            if not isinstance(checked, ResultEvent):
                continue
            state_event = StateEvent(
                execution_id=execution.execution_id, seq=seq + 1, time=now, state=final_state
            )
            return checked.execution, (state_event, checked)
        raise RuntimeError("the fallback result could not be stored")

    # Environments.

    async def _environment(self, environment_id: str) -> _Environment:
        while True:
            fence = self._daemon_fences.get(environment_id)
            if fence is not None:
                await asyncio.shield(fence)
                continue
            environment = self._environments.setdefault(environment_id, _Environment())
            if self.store.recycle_needed(environment_id):
                async with environment.lock:
                    if not self.store.recycle_needed(environment_id):
                        continue
                    fence = self._start_daemon_fence(environment_id)
                await asyncio.shield(fence)
                continue
            # Marked used before anything waits, so that suspension leaves it alone.
            environment.last_used = time.monotonic()
            if environment.channel is None or environment.channel.closed:
                # Outside the lock: preparing may start a stopped sandbox under the
                # environments' own lock, which suspension holds while it takes this one.
                await self.backend.prepare(environment_id)
            try:
                async with environment.lock:
                    if (
                        self._environments.get(environment_id) is not environment
                        or environment_id in self._daemon_fences
                    ):
                        continue  # released or fenced while this request waited
                    await self._open(environment_id, environment)
            except _DaemonIncarnationError:
                fence = self._start_daemon_fence(environment_id)
                await asyncio.shield(fence)
                continue
            return environment

    def _start_daemon_fence(self, environment_id: str) -> asyncio.Task[None]:
        self._quarantined.add(environment_id)
        fence = self._daemon_fences.get(environment_id)
        if fence is None:
            fence = self._spawn(self._recycle_daemon(environment_id))
            self._daemon_fences[environment_id] = fence
            fence.add_done_callback(partial(self._fence_done, environment_id))
        return fence

    def _fence_done(self, environment_id: str, task: asyncio.Task[None]) -> None:
        if self._daemon_fences.get(environment_id) is task:
            self._daemon_fences.pop(environment_id, None)

    async def _recycle_daemon(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Fence the whole VM, outside the execution lock, before publishing a replacement.

        OpenShell can refuse a peer's /proc/environ after its ancestor daemon dies.
        Owner-mark scans alone cannot prove its escaped children have stopped. Keep
        the old endpoint durable until the managed lifecycle confirms stop/start.
        """
        if self.recycle_daemon is None:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "executor incarnation lost; replacement refused until the sandbox is recycled",
            )
        binding = self.store.recycle_binding(environment_id)
        if binding is None:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "original sandbox identity was not recorded; replacement refused until "
                "an operator confirms cleanup of the original sandbox",
            )
        old_incarnation = self.store.endpoint_incarnation(environment_id)
        await self.recycle_daemon(environment_id, *binding)
        if old_incarnation is not None:
            # This callback proved termination of the original immutable VM
            # binding. Incarnation change/transport failure alone never clears.
            self.store.fenced_captures(environment_id, old_incarnation, *binding)
            self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()
        self.store.finish_recycle(environment_id)
        self._quarantined.discard(environment_id)

    async def _open(self, environment_id: str, environment: _Environment) -> None:
        """Start the environment's executor unless one runs. Hold its lock."""
        if environment.channel is None or environment.channel.closed:
            identity = self.daemon_identity(environment_id) if self.daemon_identity else None
            channel = await self.backend.open(
                environment_id,
                partial(self._on_event, environment_id),
                partial(self._on_closed, environment_id),
            )
            self._channels.add(channel)
            if (
                self.daemon_identity is not None
                and self.daemon_identity(environment_id) != identity
            ):
                await channel.shutdown()
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "environment binding changed during open")
            previous = self.store.endpoint_incarnation(environment_id)
            previous_binding = self.store.endpoint_binding(environment_id)
            if (
                self.backend.name == "openshell"
                and channel.daemon_token is not None
                and previous is not None
                and (
                    channel.incarnation != previous
                    or (previous_binding is not None and previous_binding != identity)
                )
            ):
                self.store.require_recycle(environment_id, previous)
                self._quarantined.add(environment_id)
                await channel.shutdown()
                for live in list(self._live.values()):
                    saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
                    if (
                        live.environment_id == environment_id
                        and live.dispatched
                        and saved is not None
                        and saved[1] == previous
                        and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
                    ):
                        self._lose(live, "the sandbox executor incarnation")
                raise _DaemonIncarnationError()
            await self._sync_package_gate(environment_id, channel)
            try:
                hostname, languages, features = self._describe(environment_id, channel.hello)
                self._observe(environment_id, channel.hello.get("environment"), "")
                self.store.kernel_starts.epoch(
                    environment_id,
                    channel.incarnation,
                    channel.hello.get("package_epoch"),
                    channel.hello.get("environment"),
                    remember=True,
                )
                declared = self.backend.isolation_tier
                isolation = await probe(channel, declared, self.state_dir)
            except Exception:
                await channel.shutdown()  # never leave an executor running unused
                raise
            if isolation.tier < declared:
                _log.warning(
                    "environment %s: isolation tier %d declared, %d in effect: %s",
                    environment_id,
                    declared,
                    isolation.tier,
                    "; ".join(isolation.evidence.findings),
                )
            environment.location = Location(
                pool_id=self.pool_id,
                backend=self.backend.name,
                sandbox_id=self.backend.sandbox_id(environment_id),
                hostname=hostname,
                isolation_tier=isolation.tier,
                declared_isolation_tier=declared,
                isolation_evidence=isolation.evidence,
            )
            environment.languages = languages
            environment.features = features
            environment.channel = channel
            if channel.daemon_token is not None:
                self.store.remember_endpoint(environment_id, channel.incarnation, identity)
            await self._reconcile_captures(environment_id, channel)

    async def forget_revisions(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Forget a deleted environment's revisions, and delete the lockfiles only they
        named: environments that are gone keep nothing in the store."""
        self.revisions.forget(environment_id)
        self.store.kernel_starts.forget(environment_id)

    async def confirm_capture_cleanup(
        self, environment_id: str, sandbox: str, sandbox_id: str
    ) -> None:
        """Trusted lifecycle callback after proof of this exact original VM's deletion.

        Active host owners retain admission even after guest cleanup is proved.
        Unknown/other bindings and corrupt state never inherit the proof.
        """
        for lease in self.store.capture_leases():
            if lease.environment_id == environment_id and (lease.sandbox, lease.sandbox_id) == (
                sandbox,
                sandbox_id,
            ):
                self.store.fenced_captures(environment_id, lease.incarnation, sandbox, sandbox_id)
        self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()

    def _package_deletion_binding(self, environment_id: str) -> str | None:
        if self.daemon_identity is not None:
            identity = self.daemon_identity(environment_id)
            return repr(identity) if identity is not None else None
        return repr(
            (
                self.backend.name,
                str(getattr(self.backend, "root", "")),
                self.backend.sandbox_id(environment_id),
            )
        )

    async def forget_package_gate(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Only confirmed deletion, after provisioning drain, may remove this fence."""
        self.store.forget_package_gate(
            environment_id, binding=self._package_deletion_binding(environment_id)
        )

    async def guard_package_deletion(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """Require original-binding proof before any explicit guest teardown."""
        self.store.guard_package_deletion(
            environment_id, self._package_deletion_binding(environment_id)
        )

    async def guard_package_reuse(self, environment_id: str) -> None:
        """A new VM cannot replace the unknown original held package binding."""
        if self.store.package_gate(
            environment_id
        ).mode != "ready" or self.store.package_gate_has_binding(environment_id):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "original package binding requires confirmed sandbox deletion",
            )

    def _want_lockfile(self, environment_id: str) -> bool:
        """Ask the executor for the current lockfile if the current revision has none, as
        revision 0 has none at first; return whether it was asked. One request at a time
        for each environment, and nothing waits for it. Executions ask (_ask_lockfile),
        each within its budget: revision 0 gets its lockfile as the first one starts."""
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel if environment is not None else None
        if (
            channel is None
            or channel.closed
            or environment_id in self._fetching
            or not self.revisions.needs_lockfile(environment_id)
        ):
            return False
        self._fetching.add(environment_id)
        task = self._spawn(self._fetch_lockfile(environment_id, channel))
        task.add_done_callback(lambda _: self._fetching.discard(environment_id))
        return True

    async def _fetch_lockfile(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        try:
            reply = await channel.request("lockfile", reply_timeout=LOCKFILE_TIMEOUT)
        except WorkerError as error:
            _log.info("environment %s: no lockfile from its executor: %s", environment_id, error)
            return
        if not self.revisions.needs_lockfile(environment_id):
            return  # a revision event brought one meanwhile
        prepared = await self._prepare(environment_id, reply.get("lockfile"))
        if prepared is None or not self.revisions.attach(
            environment_id, reply.get("fingerprint"), prepared
        ):
            _log.info("environment %s: the executor's lockfile was not kept", environment_id)

    async def _prepare(self, environment_id: str, raw: object) -> Prepared | None:
        """Check and store a lockfile from the executor, in a thread, one at a time for each
        environment: the event loop never waits for one (CP-18)."""
        if raw is None:
            return None
        lock = self._lockfile_locks.setdefault(environment_id, asyncio.Lock())
        async with lock:
            try:
                return await asyncio.to_thread(self.revisions.prepare, raw)
            except OSError as exc:
                _log.warning("environment %s: cannot store a lockfile: %s", environment_id, exc)
                return None

    def _describe(
        self, environment_id: str, hello: Message
    ) -> tuple[str, tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]:
        """The host name, kernel languages and features from an executor's ``hello``, checked."""
        where, languages = hello.get("location"), hello.get("languages", [])
        if not isinstance(where, dict) or not isinstance(languages, list):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "the executor sent a malformed hello")
        hostname = cast(dict[str, Any], where).get("hostname")
        if not isinstance(hostname, str):
            hostname = ""
        hostname = "".join(char for char in hostname[:MAX_HOSTNAME] if char.isprintable())
        if hello.get("not_dumpable") is False:
            _log.info(
                "the executor for %s stays dumpable, so research code in that environment can "
                "reach its file descriptors through /proc (the sandbox refuses sockets to a "
                "process that is not dumpable)",
                environment_id,
            )
        if hello.get("subreaper") is False:
            _log.warning(
                "the executor for %s cannot adopt orphaned processes; a shell call's processes "
                "that leave its session and clear their environment can outlive it",
                environment_id,
            )
        names = (name for name in cast(list[object], languages) if isinstance(name, str))
        raw: object = hello.get("features", [])
        offered = cast(list[object], raw) if isinstance(raw, list) else []
        features = tuple(dict.fromkeys(f for f in offered if isinstance(f, str) and f in FEATURES))
        return (
            hostname or "unknown",
            tuple(dict.fromkeys(n for n in names if n in LANGUAGES)),
            features,
        )

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def _using(self, environment_id: str) -> AsyncGenerator[ExecutorChannel]:
        """The environment's executor, counted as in use until the block ends."""
        environment = await self._environment(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel
        if channel is None:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, f"environment {environment_id} has no executor"
            )
        environment.requests += 1
        try:
            yield channel
        finally:
            environment.requests -= 1
            environment.last_used = time.monotonic()

    async def _on_closed(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        self._channels.discard(channel)
        self._gate_acked.pop(channel, None)
        if channel.daemon_token is not None and (self._closing or not channel.detaching):
            poller = self._pollers.get(environment_id)
            if poller is not None and poller[0] is channel:
                self._pollers.pop(environment_id, None)
                if poller[1] is not asyncio.current_task():
                    poller[1].cancel()
            environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
            if environment is not None and environment.channel is channel:
                environment.channel = None
            if not self._closing:
                lives = [
                    live
                    for live in self._live.values()
                    if live.channel is channel and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
                ]
                self._spawn(self._recover(environment_id, lives))
            return
        # The executions sent to this executor end with it, whether or not its
        # environment's record still names it.
        for live in list(self._live.values()):
            if live.channel is channel and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                self._lose(live, "the worker" if self._closing else "the executor")
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        if environment is not None and environment.channel is channel:
            environment.channel = None

    # Submission and dispatch.

    async def submit(
        self, request: ExecutionRequest, *, origin: str | None = None
    ) -> tuple[Execution, bool]:
        """Return the execution for ``request.operation_id``, creating it if it is new.

        ``origin`` names the provisioning operation the execution is an install step of: a
        managed change its package commands make is recorded as that operation's.
        """
        if self._closing:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "the worker is closing")
        encoded = request.model_dump_json()
        if isinstance(request, JobRequest):
            # Omitting a timeout selects policy defaults; explicitly requesting 24h does
            # not. Keep the original semantic request stable across policy changes.
            encoded += ":explicit_timeout=" + str("timeout_seconds" in request.model_fields_set)
        digest = hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode()).hexdigest()
        found = self.store.find_operation(request.context.project_id, request.operation_id)
        if found is not None:
            execution_id, existing = found
            if existing != digest:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.CONFLICT,
                    f"operation {request.operation_id} was submitted with a different request",
                )
            return self.get(execution_id), False
        self._package_origin(request, origin)
        if (
            request.context.environment_id in self._quarantined
            or request.context.environment_id in self._daemon_fences
            or self.store.recycle_needed(request.context.environment_id)
        ):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "the environment is fenced until its sandbox executor is safely recycled",
            )
        job: JobDetails | None = None
        execution_id = new_id("exe")
        if isinstance(request, JobRequest):
            context = request.context
            if (
                context.environment_id in self._released_environments
                or (context.project_id, context.environment_id, context.session_id)
                in self._closing_sessions
            ):
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "the job's session or environment is closing"
                )
            resources = (
                self.job_resources(context.environment_id) if self.job_resources else Resources()
            )
            maximum = min(
                604800.0,
                resources.job_wall_time_max.total_seconds()
                if resources.job_wall_time_max
                else 604800.0,
            )
            default = min(
                maximum,
                resources.job_wall_time_default.total_seconds()
                if resources.job_wall_time_default
                else 86400.0,
            )
            timeout = (
                request.timeout_seconds
                if "timeout_seconds" in request.model_fields_set
                else default
            )
            if timeout > maximum:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.POLICY_DENIED,
                    f"job time limit exceeds the policy maximum of {maximum:g} s",
                )
            running = self._running_jobs(context.environment_id)
            session = [
                live.execution
                for live in self._live.values()
                if live.execution.kind == "job"
                and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
                and live.execution.context.project_id == context.project_id
                and live.execution.context.session_id == context.session_id
            ]
            if len(running) >= (resources.jobs_per_environment or 8) or len(session) >= (
                resources.jobs_per_session or 4
            ):
                ids = ", ".join(dict.fromkeys(job.execution_id for job in [*running, *session]))
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.POLICY_DENIED, f"job concurrency limit reached; active jobs: {ids}"
                )
            request = request.model_copy(update={"timeout_seconds": timeout})
            job = JobDetails(
                purpose=request.purpose,
                expected_progress=request.expected_progress,
                wake_session=request.wake_session,
                timeout_seconds=timeout,
                stdout_path=f".jobs/{execution_id}/stdout.log",
                stderr_path=f".jobs/{execution_id}/stderr.log",
            )
        execution = Execution(
            execution_id=execution_id,
            attempt_id=new_id("att"),
            operation_id=request.operation_id,
            kind=request.kind,
            context=request.context,
            state=ExecutionState.QUEUED,
            submitted_at=_now(),
            origin=origin,
            job=job,
        )
        self.store.insert_execution(execution, digest)
        self.store.remember_request(execution_id, request.model_dump_json())
        live = self._track(execution, request.output_limit_bytes)
        self._state(live, ExecutionState.QUEUED)
        self.store.update_execution(live.execution)
        self._spawn(self._dispatch(live, request))
        return live.execution, True

    async def _dispatch(self, live: _Live, request: ExecutionRequest) -> None:
        """Send the request to its executor; whatever goes wrong, the execution ends."""
        try:
            await self._send(live, request)
        except WorkerError as error:
            if (
                live.dispatched
                and not isinstance(error, ExecutorRefusalError)
                and live.channel is not None
                and live.channel.daemon_token is not None
            ):
                await live.channel.close()
            else:
                self._fail(live, error.info())
        except Exception as exc:
            _log.exception("dispatching execution %s failed", live.execution.execution_id)
            self._fail(
                live,
                ErrorInfo(
                    kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL,
                    message=f"the worker could not dispatch this attempt ({type(exc).__name__})",
                ),
            )

    def _fail(self, live: _Live, error: ErrorInfo) -> None:
        environment = self._environments.get(live.environment_id)
        if environment is not None:
            environment.running.discard(live.execution.execution_id)
            environment.last_used = time.monotonic()
        self._finish(live, ExecutionState.FAILED, Result(error=error))

    async def _send(self, live: _Live, request: ExecutionRequest) -> None:
        execution_id = live.execution.execution_id
        if live.cancel_requested or live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
            self._finish(
                live,
                ExecutionState.CANCELLED,
                Result(
                    error=ErrorInfo(kind=ErrorKind.CANCELLED, message="cancelled before it started")
                ),
            )
            return
        environment = await self._environment(request.context.environment_id)
        if live.cancel_requested or live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
            self._finish(
                live,
                ExecutionState.CANCELLED,
                Result(
                    error=ErrorInfo(kind=ErrorKind.CANCELLED, message="cancelled before it started")
                ),
            )
            return
        if isinstance(request, JobRequest) and "jobs" not in environment.features:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED, "this executor does not support background jobs"
            )
        if isinstance(request, PdfRequest) and "pdf" not in environment.features:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED, "this environment cannot read PDFs (it lacks pdf_oxide)"
            )
        if isinstance(request, CellRequest) and request.language not in environment.languages:
