            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED, f"no {request.language} kernel in this environment"
            )
        self._save(live, location=self._located(request.context.environment_id, environment))
        fields: dict[str, Any] = {
            "execution": execution_id,
            "session": request.context.session_id,
            "timeout": request.timeout_seconds,
            "limit": request.output_limit_bytes,
        }
        if isinstance(request, ShellRequest | JobRequest):
            fields.update(cwd=request.cwd)
            if request.argv is not None:
                fields["argv"] = list(request.argv)
            else:
                fields["script"] = request.script
        elif isinstance(request, PdfRequest):
            fields.update(
                request.model_dump(
                    mode="json",
                    include={"operation", "path", "pages", "query", "page", "region", "dpi"}
                    | {"include_artifacts", "out"},
                    exclude_none=True,
                )
            )
        else:
            fields.update(language=request.language, code=request.code)
        channel = environment.channel
        if channel is None:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "the executor went away")
        environment.running.add(execution_id)
        if self.shared is not None:
            live.notices += await self._sync(self.shared.down, request.context, channel)
            if live.cancel_requested:  # while the shared files synced
                self._finish(
                    live,
                    ExecutionState.CANCELLED,
                    Result(
                        error=ErrorInfo(
                            kind=ErrorKind.CANCELLED, message="cancelled before it started"
                        ),
                        notices=tuple(live.notices),
                    ),
                )
                return
        self._package_origin(request, live.execution.origin)
        if not await self._sync_package_gate(request.context.environment_id, channel):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                "legacy executor lacks package admission fencing; protected work refused",
            )
        gate = self.store.package_gate(request.context.environment_id)
        self._package_origin(request, live.execution.origin)
        if live.execution.origin is not None:
            fields.update(
                package_operation=live.execution.origin, package_generation=gate.generation
            )
        live.dispatched = True
        live.dispatched_at = time.monotonic()
        live.channel = channel
        identity = self.daemon_identity(live.environment_id) if self.daemon_identity else None
        if channel.daemon_token is not None and (
            self.store.endpoint_incarnation(live.environment_id) != channel.incarnation
            or self.store.endpoint_binding(live.environment_id) != identity
        ):
            identity = None  # never combine this channel with a newer endpoint's identity
        self.store.observation_dispatch(
            live.execution, channel.incarnation, identity, daemon=channel.daemon_token is not None
        )
        live.watchdog = self._spawn(self._watch(live, request.timeout_seconds))
        await channel.request(request.kind, **fields)
        if channel.daemon_token is not None:
            self._poll(request.context.environment_id, channel)

    async def _watch(self, live: _Live, timeout: float) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(max(0, timeout + WATCHDOG_GRACE))
        if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES or live.final is not None:
            return
        _log.warning("execution %s overran its limit; cancelling it", live.execution.execution_id)
        with contextlib.suppress(WorkerError):
            await self.cancel(live.execution.execution_id)
        await asyncio.sleep(LOST_GRACE)
        self._finish(
            live,
            ExecutionState.LOST,
            Result(
                error=ErrorInfo(
                    kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL, message="the executor never reported a result"
                )
            ),
        )

    async def _on_event(self, environment_id: str, message: Message) -> None:
        execution_id = message.get("execution")
        live = self._live.get(execution_id) if isinstance(execution_id, str) else None
        # Only the executor an execution was sent to may report on it.
        if (
            live is None
            or live.environment_id != environment_id
            or not live.dispatched
            or live.channel is None
            or live.final is not None  # it ended; only its sync is left
            or live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES
        ):
            return
        source = message.get("source_seq")
        if live.channel.daemon_token is not None:
            if message.get("_bridge") != live.channel.bridge_id:
                return
            saved = self.store.recovery(live.execution.execution_id)
            previous = saved[2] if saved else 0
            if not isinstance(source, int) or isinstance(source, bool) or not 0 < source < 2**62:
                return
            if source <= previous:
                return
            source_from = message.get("source_from")
            if source != previous + 1 and (
                not isinstance(source_from, int)
                or isinstance(source_from, bool)
                or source_from != previous + 1
            ):
                self._lose(live, "the executor with an invalid replay range")
                return
        token = _SOURCE_EVENT.set(
            (live.execution.execution_id, source)
            if isinstance(source, int)
            and not isinstance(source, bool)
            and live.channel.daemon_token
            else None
        )
        try:
            if message.get("event") == "revision":
                # Its lockfile is checked in a thread; this executor's next events wait.
                await self._revised(environment_id, live, message)
            else:
                self._apply(live, environment_id, message)
            if (
                isinstance(source, int)
                and message.get("event") != "end"
                and live.channel.daemon_token
            ):
                self.store.source_cursor(live.execution.execution_id, source)
        except Exception:
            _log.exception("execution %s: an event from the executor failed", execution_id)
            if message.get("event") == "end":  # the execution must end all the same
                self._finish(
                    live,
                    ExecutionState.FAILED,
                    Result(
                        error=ErrorInfo(
                            kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL, message="the executor's result was unusable"
                        )
                    ),
                )
        finally:
            _SOURCE_EVENT.reset(token)

    def _apply(self, live: _Live, environment_id: str, message: Message) -> None:
        execution_id = live.execution.execution_id
        kind = message.get("event")
        if kind == "state" and message.get("state") == "running":
            if live.execution.state is ExecutionState.QUEUED:
                update: dict[str, Any] = {"state": ExecutionState.RUNNING, "started_at": _now()}
                # The revision as it started, which waiting for a package command can change.
                location = live.execution.location
                if location is not None and "environment" in message:
                    revision = self._observe(environment_id, message.get("environment"), "")
                    if revision is not None:
                        update["location"] = location.model_copy(
                            update={"environment_revision": str(revision)}
                        )
                event = StateEvent(
                    execution_id=execution_id,
                    seq=live.execution.last_seq + 1,
                    time=_now(),
                    state=ExecutionState.RUNNING,
                )

                def start() -> Execution:
                    kernel, kernel_state_lost = self._kernel(
                        environment_id,
                        live.execution.context.session_id,
                        message.get("kernel"),
                        False,
                        project_id=live.execution.context.project_id,
                        birth_execution=execution_id if not live.reattached else None,
                        fingerprint=message.get("environment"),
                        expected_channel=live.channel,
                    )
                    if kernel is not None and live.execution.kind == "cell":
                        update.update(
                            kernel=kernel,
                            kernel_state_lost=live.execution.kernel_state_lost or kernel_state_lost,
                        )
                    return live.execution.model_copy(update={**update, "last_seq": event.seq})

                source = _SOURCE_EVENT.get()
                acknowledged = (
                    source[1] if source is not None and source[0] == execution_id else None
                )
                live.execution = self.store.commit_kernel_start(start, event, acknowledged)
                self._changed(live)
                self._ask_lockfile(environment_id, live)
        elif kind == "stream":
            name = "stderr" if message.get("name") == "stderr" else "stdout"
            text = message.get("text")
            if not isinstance(text, str) or not text or not self._admit(live, _size(text)):
                return
            self._emit(
                live,
                lambda seq, time: StreamEvent(
                    execution_id=execution_id, seq=seq, time=time, name=name, text=text
                ),
            )
        elif kind == "output":
            try:
                output = RichOutput.model_validate(message.get("output"))
            except ValidationError:
                _log.warning("execution %s: malformed output dropped", execution_id)
                return
            if not self._admit(live, sum(_size(value) for value in output.data.values())):
                return
            self._emit(
                live,
                lambda seq, time: OutputEvent(
                    execution_id=execution_id, seq=seq, time=time, output=output
                ),
            )
        elif kind == "end":
            # Observation data is derived and independent of the research result. A
            # bad sidecar must never enter the result parser's FAILED fallback.
            live.observation, live.observation_gap = normalize_observation(
                message.get("output_observations")
            )
            if message.get("observation_omitted") == "oversized":
                live.observation, live.observation_gap = None, "oversized"
            try:
                state = ExecutionState(str(message.get("state")))
                if state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                    raise ValueError(state)
                raw = message.get("result")
                fields = cast(dict[str, Any], raw) if isinstance(raw, dict) else {}
                result = self._result(environment_id, live, fields)
            except Exception as exc:  # the execution must end whatever the executor sent
                state = ExecutionState.FAILED
                result = Result(
                    error=ErrorInfo(
                        kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL,
                        message=f"malformed result from the executor: {str(exc)[:500]}",
                    )
                )
            if live.overflowed and state is ExecutionState.CANCELLED:
                result = result.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "error": ErrorInfo(
                            kind=ErrorKind.CANCELLED,
                            message="cancelled by the worker: the executor sent more output "
                            "than the output limit allows",
                        )
                    }
                )
            if message.get("recovery_compacted") is True:
                live.notices.append(
                    "The executor retained a compact recovery result after journal pressure; "
                    "whole job stdout/stderr logs remain in the workspace."
                )
            source = _SOURCE_EVENT.get()
            live.final_source_seq = source[1] if source is not None else None
            live.final = (state, result)
            if live.cancel_watchdog is not None:
                live.cancel_watchdog.cancel()
            live.ended_at = time.monotonic()
            if self.shared is None or live.channel is None:
                self._complete(live, live.notices)
            else:
                if live.watchdog is not None:
                    live.watchdog.cancel()  # the attempt is over; only the sync is left
                    live.watchdog = None
                self._spawn(self._end(live, live.channel))

    async def _end(self, live: _Live, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        """Copy the shared files the attempt changed into the project's copy, then end it (D79).

        A later call in another environment of the project then finds them there.
        """
        notices = list(live.notices)
        if self.shared is not None:
            notices += await self._sync(self.shared.up, live.execution.context, channel)
        try:
            self._complete(live, notices)
        except Exception:
            # The attempt must end all the same; the watchdog no longer watches it.
            _log.exception(
                "execution %s: its result could not be stored", live.execution.execution_id
            )
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                self._finish(
                    live,
                    ExecutionState.FAILED,
                    Result(
                        error=ErrorInfo(
                            kind=ErrorKind.INTERNAL,
                            message="the attempt's result could not be stored",
                        )
                    ),
                )

    def _complete(self, live: _Live, notices: list[str]) -> None:
        """End the attempt with the outcome the executor reported, and the sync's notices."""
        if live.final is None:
            return
        state, result = live.final
        context = live.execution.context
        held = self._held_notices.pop((context.environment_id, context.session_id), [])
        changes: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if held or notices:
            changes["notices"] = (*result.notices, *held, *notices)
        if self.shared is not None and result.written_files:
            # Files the sync wrote during the call, unchanged since, are not the call's own.
            synced = self.shared.unchanged_writes(
                live.environment_id, result.written_files, live.dispatched_at, live.ended_at
            )
            if synced:
                changes["written_files"] = tuple(
                    path for path in result.written_files if path not in synced
                )
        self._finish(live, state, result.model_copy(update=changes) if changes else result)

    async def _sync_shared(
        self, context: ExecutionContext, path: str, channel: ExecutorChannel
    ) -> None:
        """Bring the shared files up to date before a file request that reads them (D79)."""
        if self.shared is None or not _in_shared(path):
            return
        self._tell(context, await self._sync(self.shared.down, context, channel))

    def _tell(self, context: ExecutionContext, notices: list[str]) -> None:
        """Pass on what syncing for a file request found (D79).

        The calls running in the environment get it with their results, since a change of
        theirs may be what it is about; the requesting session gets it with its next
        result there, unless one of those calls is its own.
        """
        if not notices:
            return
        told = False
        for live in self._live.values():
            running = live.execution.context
            if (
                live.environment_id == context.environment_id
                and running.project_id == context.project_id  # never another project's
                and live.dispatched
                and live.final is None
                and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
            ):
                live.notices = _held([*live.notices, *notices])
                told = told or running.session_id == context.session_id
        if not told:
            key = (context.environment_id, context.session_id)
            held = self._held_notices.pop(key, [])
            self._held_notices[key] = _held([*held, *notices])
            while len(self._held_notices) > MAX_HELD_SESSIONS:
                self._held_notices.popitem(last=False)

    async def _sync(
        self,
        step: Callable[[str, str, str, ExecutorChannel], Awaitable[list[str]]],
        context: ExecutionContext,
        channel: ExecutorChannel,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Run one step of the shared files' sync; its failure never fails the call (D79)."""
        try:
            return await asyncio.wait_for(
                step(context.project_id, context.environment_id, context.session_id, channel),
                SHARED_TIMEOUT,
            )
        except Exception as exc:  # the call goes on with shared/ as it is
            _log.warning(
                "syncing the shared files of %s in %s failed: %s",
                context.project_id,
                context.environment_id,
                exc,
            )
            return [_UNSYNCED]

    def _admit(self, live: _Live, size: int) -> bool:
        """Charge one stream or output event to the execution's budget; False once spent.

        Past the event count, events are only dropped; past the byte budget, which
        an honest executor never reaches, the attempt is also cancelled.
        """
        live.events += 1
        live.stored += size
        if live.stored > OUTPUT_BUDGET * live.limit + 65536:
            if not live.overflowed:
                live.overflowed = True
                _log.warning(
                    "execution %s: the executor sent more output than its limit; cancelling it",
                    live.execution.execution_id,
                )
                self._spawn(self._cancel_quietly(live))
            return False
        if live.events == MAX_EVENTS + 1:
            _log.warning(
                "execution %s: over %d events; dropping the rest",
                live.execution.execution_id,
                MAX_EVENTS,
            )
        return live.events <= MAX_EVENTS

    async def _cancel_quietly(self, live: _Live) -> None:
        with contextlib.suppress(WorkerError):
            await self.cancel(live.execution.execution_id)

    def _result(self, environment_id: str, live: _Live, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> Result:
        """The executor's result, checked and bounded by the attempt's output limit."""
        after = self._revision_after(environment_id, live, raw)
        kernel, lost = self._kernel(
            environment_id,
            live.execution.context.session_id,
            raw.get("kernel"),
            raw.get("state_lost") is True or live.execution.kernel_state_lost,
            project_id=live.execution.context.project_id,
            expected_channel=live.channel,
        )
        pinned = live.execution.kernel
        if (
            kernel is not None
            and pinned is not None
            and (kernel.kernel_id, kernel.language, kernel.generation)
            == (pinned.kernel_id, pinned.language, pinned.generation)
        ):
            revision = kernel.current_revision
            start_revision = pinned.start_revision
            if start_revision is not None and revision is not None and start_revision > revision:
                start_revision = None
            status = (
                "unknown"
                if start_revision is None or revision is None
                else ("current" if start_revision == revision else "predates")
            )
            kernel = kernel.model_copy(
                update={"start_revision": start_revision, "revision_status": status}
            )
        running = self._session_kernel_info(
            live.execution.context, raw.get("running_kernels"), expected_channel=live.channel
        )
        written = raw.get("written_files")
        paths = [
            path
            for path in (cast(list[object], written) if isinstance(written, list) else [])
            if isinstance(path, str)
            and path
            and len(path.encode("utf-8", "replace")) <= MAX_PATH_BYTES
        ]
        location = live.execution.location
        before = location.environment_revision if location is not None else None
        return Result(
            exit_code=_integer(raw.get("exit_code")),
            signal=_integer(raw.get("signal"), 1, 255),
            status=raw.get("status"),
            execution_count=_integer(raw.get("execution_count"), 0),
            stdout=_stream(raw.get("stdout"), "stdout", live.limit),
            stderr=_stream(raw.get("stderr"), "stderr", live.limit),
            outputs=_outputs(raw.get("outputs"), live.limit),
            error=_error(raw.get("error")),
            kernel=kernel,
            running_kernels=running,
            state_lost=lost,
            elapsed_seconds=_seconds(raw.get("elapsed_seconds")),
            sandbox_started_at=_epoch(raw.get("sandbox_started")),
            sandbox_ended_at=_epoch(raw.get("sandbox_ended")),
            written_files=tuple(paths[:MAX_WRITTEN]),
            written_files_truncated=raw.get("written_files_truncated") is True
            or len(paths) > MAX_WRITTEN,
            environment_revision=after,
            overlapping_change=raw.get("environment_changing") is True
            or (before is not None and after is not None and before != after),
            notices=self._notices(environment_id, live),
        )

    def _notices(self, environment_id: str, live: _Live) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Admission notices the session has not seen, each once (D69).

        A session's first result starts from its submission; later ones from the last
        notice it received, since decisions are stamped when they are recorded.
        """
        if self.notices is None:
            return ()
        key = (environment_id, live.execution.context.session_id)
        since = self._noticed.get(key, live.execution.submitted_at)
        try:
            fresh = self.notices(environment_id, since)
        except Exception:
            _log.exception("could not read the admission notices of %s", environment_id)
            return ()
        self._noticed[key] = max([since, *(at for at, _ in fresh)])
        return tuple(text for _, text in fresh)

    def _located(self, environment_id: str, environment: _Environment) -> Location | None:
        """The environment's location, with its current revision."""
        location, record = environment.location, self.store.revision(environment_id)
        if location is None or record is None:
            return location
        return location.model_copy(update={"environment_revision": str(record.revision)})

    def _revision_after(self, environment_id: str, live: _Live, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """The environment's revision once the attempt's fingerprint is counted. A change
        seen only here is unmanaged, so it is no provisioning operation's, even when the
        execution is one's step."""
        revision = self._observe(environment_id, raw.get("environment"), live.execution.attempt_id)
        self._ask_lockfile(environment_id, live)
        return None if revision is None else str(revision)

    def _observe(self, environment_id: str, fingerprint: object, changed_by: str) -> int | None:
        """The environment's revision after the executor reported ``fingerprint`` (W3).

        The first fingerprint is revision 0, and each different one counts one up,
        recorded against the attempt that reported it (empty between executors). The
        executor reports each change in a ``revision`` event first, so a new fingerprint
        here is one it could not account for. The executor is untrusted: research code
        can only make its own environment's revisions count up.
        """
        return self.revisions.observe(environment_id, fingerprint, changed_by)

    async def _revised(self, environment_id: str, live: _Live, message: Message) -> None:
        """A change to the environment's packages that the executor saw (CP-4, CP-16).

        A managed change names the attempt that ran its package commands, which must be
        one of this environment's; an unmanaged one, the attempt after which it was seen.
        The executor sends a lockfile with each attempt's last change. The worker keeps
        one for each attempt, and checks at most MAX_EXECUTION_LOCKFILES for each
        execution, those it asks for included. A revision left without one gets the
        current lockfile asked for, while it is current.
        """
        live.revisions += 1
        if live.revisions > MAX_REVISIONS:
            if live.revisions == MAX_REVISIONS + 1:
                _log.warning(
                    "execution %s: over %d revisions; dropping the rest",
                    live.execution.execution_id,
                    MAX_REVISIONS,
                )
            return
        managed = message.get("managed")
        cause = message.get("cause")
        attempt, origin = (
            self._attempt(environment_id, cause) if isinstance(cause, str) else ("", None)
        )
        prepared: Prepared | None = None
        raw = message.get("lockfile")
        if (
            raw is not None
            and attempt
            and attempt not in live.lockfile_attempts
            and live.lockfiles < MAX_EXECUTION_LOCKFILES
        ):
            live.lockfiles += 1
            live.lockfile_attempts.add(attempt)
            prepared = await self._prepare(environment_id, raw)
        commands, omitted = (
            package_commands(message.get("commands"), message.get("omitted_commands"))
            if managed is True
            else ((), 0)
        )
        self.revisions.observe(
            environment_id,
            message.get("fingerprint"),
            attempt,
            managed=managed if isinstance(managed, bool) else None,
            commands=commands,
            omitted=omitted,
            lockfile=prepared,
            # Only a change its own package commands made is the operation's.
            operation=origin if managed is True else None,
        )
        if (
            live.channel is not None
            and self._environments.get(environment_id) is not None
            and self._environments[environment_id].channel is live.channel
        ):
            self.store.kernel_starts.epoch(
                environment_id,
                live.channel.incarnation,
                message.get("package_epoch"),
                message.get("fingerprint"),
                remember=True,
            )
        self._ask_lockfile(environment_id, live)

    def _ask_lockfile(self, environment_id: str, live: _Live) -> None:
        """Ask for the current lockfile on behalf of ``live``, within its budget: every
        lockfile checked counts, those an execution's start and end ask for too."""
        if live.lockfiles < MAX_EXECUTION_LOCKFILES and self._want_lockfile(environment_id):
            live.lockfiles += 1

    def _attempt(self, environment_id: str, execution_id: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
        """The current attempt of one of the environment's executions, and the provisioning
        operation it is a step of; empty for any other execution."""
        if not _EXECUTION.fullmatch(execution_id):
            return "", None
        live = self._live.get(execution_id)
        try:
            execution = live.execution if live is not None else self.store.execution(execution_id)
        except ValidationError:
            return "", None
        if execution is None or execution.context.environment_id != environment_id:
            return "", None
        return execution.attempt_id, execution.origin

    def _kernel(
        self,
        environment_id: str,
        session_id: str,
        raw: object,
        state_lost: bool,
        *,
        project_id: str | None = None,
        birth_execution: str | None = None,
        fingerprint: object = None,
        restarted: bool = False,
        expected_channel: ExecutorChannel | None = None,
        remember: bool = True,
    ) -> tuple[KernelInfo | None, bool]:
        """Map the executor's kernel generation onto one that never goes back."""
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            return None, state_lost
        raw = cast(dict[str, Any], raw)
        language = raw.get("language", "python")
        generation = _integer(raw.get("generation", 1), 1, 2**31 - 1)
        if language not in LANGUAGES or generation is None:
            return None, state_lost
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel if environment is not None else None
        if expected_channel is not None and channel is not expected_channel:
            return None, state_lost  # old bridge cannot rebind a replacement's kernel
        incarnation = channel.incarnation if channel is not None else "unknown"
        try:
            record = self.store.kernel(environment_id, session_id, language)
        except ValueError:
            return None, state_lost  # damaged derived metadata cannot fail a shell result
        if record is None:
            base = 0
        elif record.incarnation != incarnation:
            # A new executor: its kernels start over, and earlier state is gone.
            base, state_lost = record.last, state_lost or record.last > 0
        else:
            base = record.base
        if base + generation > 2**62:
            return None, state_lost
        if remember:
            self.store.save_kernel(
                environment_id,
                session_id,
                language,
                KernelRecord(
                    incarnation, base, max(base + generation, record.last if record else 0)
                ),
            )
        info = {
            "kernel_id": raw.get("kernel_id"),
            "language": language,
            "generation": base + generation,
        }
        try:
            kernel = KernelInfo.model_validate(info)
        except ValidationError:
            # Not an identifier the worker can report: name the kernel after its session.
            digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{session_id}\0{language}".encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
            kernel = KernelInfo.model_validate({**info, "kernel_id": f"krn-{digest}"})
        current = self.store.kernel_starts.current(environment_id)
        revision = current[0] if current is not None else None
        kernel = kernel.model_copy(update={"current_revision": revision})
        start_environment = raw.get("start_environment")
        can_pin = (
            current is not None
            and current[1] == start_environment
            and self.store.kernel_starts.epoch(
                environment_id, incarnation, raw.get("start_package_epoch"), start_environment
            )
            == revision
            and (
                (
                    birth_execution is not None
                    and raw.get("start_execution") == birth_execution
                    and fingerprint == start_environment
                )
                or restarted
            )
        )
        if project_id is not None and channel is not None and not channel.closed:
            binding = None
            if channel.daemon_token is not None:
                endpoint = self.store.lineage_endpoint(environment_id)
                if endpoint is not None and endpoint[0] == incarnation:
                    binding = endpoint[1:]
                if binding is None and self.daemon_identity is not None:
                    can_pin = False  # a managed VM's original binding must be known
            try:
                birth = KernelBirth.model_validate(
                    {
                        "project_id": project_id,
                        "environment_id": environment_id,
                        "session_id": session_id,
                        "language": language,
                        "incarnation": incarnation,
                        "kernel_id": kernel.kernel_id,
                        "sandbox": binding[0] if binding else None,
                        "sandbox_id": binding[1] if binding else None,
                        "generation": generation,
                        "birth_id": raw.get("birth_id"),
                        "start_revision": revision if can_pin else None,
                    }
                )
            except ValidationError:
                pass  # legacy or malformed sandbox birth: do not infer it from today's packages
            else:
                kernel = self.store.kernel_starts.observe(
                    birth, kernel, revision, remember=remember
                )
        return kernel, state_lost

    def _session_kernel_info(
        self,
        context: ExecutionContext,
        raw: object,
        *,
        expected_channel: ExecutorChannel | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[KernelInfo, ...]:
        if not isinstance(raw, list):
            return ()
        raw = cast(list[object], raw)
        if len(raw) > len(LANGUAGES):
            return ()
        found: dict[str, KernelInfo] = {}
        for item in raw:
            kernel, _ = self._kernel(
                context.environment_id,
                context.session_id,
                item,
                False,
                project_id=context.project_id,
                expected_channel=expected_channel,
                remember=False,
            )
            if kernel is not None:
                found[kernel.language] = kernel
        return tuple(found.values())

    async def kernel_status(self, request: KernelStatusRequest) -> KernelListing:
        """Observe only the authenticated context's kernels; admission gates stay unchanged."""
        context = request.context
        async with self._using(context.environment_id) as channel:
            if (
                type(channel.hello.get("kernel_revision_protocol")) is not int
                or channel.hello.get("kernel_revision_protocol") != 1
            ):
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED, "legacy executor lacks scoped kernel status"
                )
            reply = await channel.request("kernels", session=context.session_id)
            return self._kernel_listing(context, channel, reply.get("kernels"))

    def _kernel_listing(
        self, context: ExecutionContext, channel: ExecutorChannel, raw: object
    ) -> KernelListing:
        if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(cast(list[object], raw)) > len(LANGUAGES):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent invalid kernel status")
        for item in cast(list[object], raw):
            if not isinstance(item, dict):
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent invalid kernel identity")
            item = cast(dict[str, object], item)
            generation = item.get("generation")
            if type(generation) is not int or not 1 <= generation < 2**31:
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent invalid kernel generation")
            try:
                KernelInfo.model_validate(
                    {key: item.get(key) for key in ("kernel_id", "language", "generation")}
                )
            except ValidationError as exc:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent invalid kernel identity"
                ) from exc
        kernels = self._session_kernel_info(
            context, cast(list[object], raw), expected_channel=channel
        )
        if len(kernels) != len(cast(list[object], raw)):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent invalid kernel identities")
        current = self.store.kernel_starts.current(context.environment_id)
        return KernelListing(
            environment_id=context.environment_id,
            session_id=context.session_id,
            current_revision=current[0] if current is not None else None,
            kernels=kernels,
        )

    def _observed_environment(
        self, context: ExecutionContext
    ) -> tuple[_Environment, ExecutorChannel]:
        environment_id = context.environment_id
        environment = self._environments.get(environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel if environment is not None else None
        if (
            self._closing
            or environment_id in self._recovering
            or environment_id in self._daemon_fences
            or environment_id in self._quarantined
            or environment_id in self._released_environments
            or (context.project_id, environment_id, context.session_id) in self._closing_sessions
            or self.store.recycle_needed(environment_id)
            or environment is None
            or environment.lock.locked()
            or channel is None
            or channel.closed
            or channel.detaching
        ):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "kernel observation needs an existing healthy connection"
            )
        return environment, channel

    def enroll_run_kernel(
        self, scope: RunKernelScope, operation_id: str, *, initialize: bool = False
    ) -> RunKernelEnrollment:
        """Retain explicit controller attribution on an existing managed VM.

        This internal observation grants no execution or kernel access. No public
        route, launcher or model tool supplies its authority. Nothing is opened,
        reconnected, started or kept alive; the caller owns synchronous Store work.
        The caller must derive the genuine run and scope from its admitted control
        context; these checks cannot establish that admission on their own.
        """
        try:
            scope = checked_run_kernel_scope(scope)
        except (ValueError, ValidationError):
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST, "invalid original run/kernel scope"
            ) from None
        context = ExecutionContext(
            project_id=scope.project_id,
            session_id=scope.session_id,
            environment_id=scope.environment_id,
        )
        environment, channel = self._observed_environment(context)
        records = RunKernelBindings(self.store)

        def observed_binding() -> RunKernelBinding:
            managed = self.daemon_identity(scope.environment_id) if self.daemon_identity else None
            if channel.daemon_token is None or type(managed) is not tuple or len(managed) != 2:
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "original managed run endpoint is unknown")
            try:
                return checked_run_kernel_binding(
                    RunKernelBinding.model_construct(
                        scope=scope,
                        sandbox=managed[0],
                        sandbox_id=managed[1],
                        incarnation=channel.incarnation,
                    )
                )
            except (ValueError, ValidationError):
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "original managed run endpoint is unknown"
                ) from None

        binding = observed_binding()
        expected = (binding.incarnation, binding.sandbox, binding.sandbox_id)

        def validate() -> None:
            current_environment, current_channel = self._observed_environment(context)
            if (
                current_environment is not environment
                or current_channel is not channel
                or channel.incarnation != binding.incarnation
                or records.endpoint(scope.environment_id) != expected
                or observed_binding() != binding
            ):
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "original managed run endpoint changed")

        value = records.enroll(binding, operation_id, initialize=initialize, validate=validate)
        validate()  # postcommit failure keeps the original audit; no automatic re-enrollment
        return value

    async def observe_kernels(self, request: KernelStatusRequest) -> KernelObservation:
        """Read an existing channel without keeping it alive or waiting on its lifecycle."""
        return await self._passive_kernels(request, self._kernel_observation)

    def _kernel_observation(
        self, context: ExecutionContext, channel: ExecutorChannel, raw: object
    ) -> KernelObservation:
        listing = self._kernel_listing(context, channel, raw)
        return KernelObservation(**listing.model_dump(), observed_at=_now())

    async def observe_kernel_lineage(
        self, request: KernelStatusRequest
    ) -> KernelLineageObservation:
        """Passive original-birth evidence; missing history is unknown, never backfilled."""
        return await self._passive_kernels(request, self._kernel_lineage)

    def _kernel_lineage(
        self, context: ExecutionContext, channel: ExecutorChannel, raw: object
    ) -> KernelLineageObservation:
        listing = self._kernel_listing(context, channel, raw)
        endpoint = self.store.lineage_endpoint(context.environment_id)
        managed = self.daemon_identity(context.environment_id) if self.daemon_identity else None
        entries: list[KernelLineageEntry] = []
        # _kernel_listing already validates raw shape, languages and generation.
        by_language = {item["language"]: item for item in cast(list[dict[str, object]], raw)}
        for kernel in listing.kernels:
            birth, reason = self.store.kernel_starts.retained(
                context.environment_id, context.session_id, kernel.language
            )
            if birth is not None:
                item = by_language[kernel.language]
                if (
                    birth.project_id != context.project_id
                    or birth.incarnation != channel.incarnation
                    or (birth.kernel_id, birth.generation, birth.birth_id)
                    != (item.get("kernel_id"), item.get("generation"), item.get("birth_id"))
                ):
                    reason = "identity_mismatch"
                elif (
                    channel.daemon_token is None
                    or birth.sandbox is None
                    or endpoint != (birth.incarnation, birth.sandbox, birth.sandbox_id)
                    or managed != (birth.sandbox, birth.sandbox_id)
                ):
                    reason = "binding_unavailable"
                else:
                    try:
                        generation = self.store.kernel(
                            context.environment_id, context.session_id, kernel.language
                        )
                    except ValueError:
                        generation = None
                    if (
                        generation is None
                        or generation.incarnation != birth.incarnation
                        or generation.base + birth.generation != kernel.generation
                        or generation.last < kernel.generation
                    ):
                        reason = "generation_unavailable"
                    elif (
                        birth.start_revision is None
                        or birth.start_revision != kernel.start_revision
                    ):
                        reason = "unknown_start_revision"
            entries.append(
                KernelLineageEntry(
                    kernel=kernel,
                    birth=birth if reason is None else None,
                    lineage_status="proved" if reason is None else "unknown",
                    unknown_reason=reason,
                )
            )
        return KernelLineageObservation(
            project_id=context.project_id,
            environment_id=context.environment_id,
            session_id=context.session_id,
            current_revision=listing.current_revision,
            kernels=tuple(entries),
            observed_at=_now(),
        )

    async def _passive_kernels(
        self,
        request: KernelStatusRequest,
        build: Callable[[ExecutionContext, ExecutorChannel, object], _Observation],
    ) -> _Observation:
        """One bounded admission lane and close token for every passive kernel consumer."""
        context = request.context
        environment_id = context.environment_id
        environment, channel = self._observed_environment(context)
        if (
            environment_id in self._kernel_observations
            or len(self._kernel_observations) >= MAX_KERNEL_OBSERVATIONS
        ):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "kernel observation capacity is busy")
        if (
            type(channel.hello.get("kernel_revision_protocol")) is not int
            or channel.hello.get("kernel_revision_protocol") != 1
        ):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED, "legacy executor lacks scoped kernel status")
        incarnation = channel.incarnation
        observer = _KernelObserver((context.project_id, environment_id, context.session_id))
        self._kernel_observations[environment_id] = observer
        try:
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(KERNEL_OBSERVATION_TIMEOUT):
                    reply = await channel.request(
                        "kernels",
                        session=context.session_id,
                        reply_timeout=KERNEL_OBSERVATION_TIMEOUT,
                    )
            except TimeoutError as exc:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "kernel observation deadline expired"
                ) from exc
            current_environment, current_channel = self._observed_environment(context)
            if (
                not observer.valid
                or current_environment is not environment
                or current_channel is not channel
                or channel.incarnation != incarnation
            ):
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "kernel observation connection changed")
            try:
                return build(context, channel, reply.get("kernels"))
            except ValidationError as exc:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "executor sent incoherent kernel observation"
                ) from exc
        finally:
            self._kernel_observations.pop(environment_id)

    # Queries and control.

    def get(self, execution_id: str, project_id: str | None = None) -> Execution:
        """The execution, which must belong to ``project_id`` when one is given."""
        live = self._live.get(execution_id)
        if live is not None:
            execution = live.execution
        else:
            try:
                found = self.store.execution(execution_id)
            except ValidationError as exc:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.INTERNAL, f"the stored record of {execution_id} is unreadable"
                ) from exc
            if found is None:
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.NOT_FOUND, f"no execution {execution_id}")
            execution = found
        if project_id is not None and execution.context.project_id != project_id:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.NOT_FOUND, f"no execution {execution_id}")
        return execution

    async def _cancel_jobs(self, jobs: list[Execution]) -> None:
        """Bound cancel acknowledgments and process completion together, including broken peers."""
        if not jobs:
            return

        async def cancel_all() -> None:
            await asyncio.gather(*(self.cancel(job.execution_id) for job in jobs))
            await asyncio.gather(*(self.wait(job.execution_id) for job in jobs))

        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(cancel_all(), CANCEL_GRACE)
        except (TimeoutError, WorkerError):
            channels: set[ExecutorChannel] = set()
            for job in jobs:
                live = self._live.get(job.execution_id)
                if live is not None and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                    if live.channel is not None:
                        channels.add(live.channel)
                    self._lose(live, "the executor that did not confirm job cancellation")
            await asyncio.gather(*(channel.shutdown() for channel in channels))

    def _running_jobs(self, environment_id: str) -> list[Execution]:
        return [
            live.execution
            for live in self._live.values()
            if live.environment_id == environment_id
            and live.execution.kind == "job"
            and live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES
        ]

    def jobs(
        self, context: ExecutionContext, limit: int = 100, after: str | None = None
    ) -> JobListing:
        """List only the requested session's jobs, including recently ended attempts."""
        if not 1 <= limit <= 500:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST, "job listing limit must be between 1 and 500"
            )
        try:
            jobs = self.store.session_jobs(context, limit + 1, after)
        except LookupError as exc:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.NOT_FOUND, "no job listing cursor for this session"
            ) from exc
        selected: list[Execution] = []
        total = 0
        for job in jobs[:limit]:
            size = len(job.model_dump_json().encode())
            if total + size > 1024 * 1024:
                break
            selected.append(job)
            total += size
        return JobListing(
            jobs=tuple(selected),
            truncated=len(jobs) > len(selected),
            next_after=selected[-1].execution_id if selected else after,
        )

    async def job_status(self, execution_id: str, project_id: str | None = None) -> JobStatus:
        """Read bounded live output without opening a new executor or waiting for the job."""
        execution = self.get(execution_id, project_id)
        if execution.kind != "job":
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.NOT_FOUND, f"no job {execution_id}")
        result = execution.result
        if result is not None:
            error = result.error
            if error is not None:
                error = ErrorInfo(kind=error.kind, message=_text(error.message, 4096) or "")
            compact = result.model_copy(
                update={
                    "stdout": None,
                    "stderr": None,
                    "outputs": (),
                    "written_files": (),
                    "notices": (),
                    "error": error,
                }
            )
            return JobStatus(
                execution=execution.model_copy(update={"result": compact}),
                stdout=_job_stream(result.stdout),
                stderr=_job_stream(result.stderr),
            )
        live = self._live.get(execution_id)
        channel = live.channel if live is not None else None
        if live is None or channel is None or channel.closed:
            return JobStatus(execution=execution)
        reply = await channel.request("job_status", execution=execution_id, reply_timeout=10)
        cpu = reply.get("cpu_seconds")
        cpu = (
            float(cpu)
            if isinstance(cpu, int | float) and not isinstance(cpu, bool) and 0 <= cpu <= 1e15
            else None
        )
        memory = _integer(reply.get("memory_bytes"), 0, 2**62)
        execution = self.get(execution_id)
        if execution.result is not None:
            return await self.job_status(execution_id, project_id)
        return JobStatus(
            execution=execution,
            stdout=_stream(reply.get("stdout"), "stdout", min(live.limit, 16384)),
            stderr=_stream(reply.get("stderr"), "stderr", min(live.limit, 16384)),
            cpu_seconds=cpu,
            memory_bytes=memory,
        )

    async def events(
        self, execution_id: str, after: int, *, heartbeat: float | None = None
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event | None, None]:
        """Yield the events after ``after``, then new ones, ending with the result.

        While nothing happens, ``None`` comes every ``heartbeat`` seconds. The
        stream also ends when the execution is over, whatever ``after`` was.
        """
        self.get(execution_id)
        while True:
            live = self._live.get(execution_id)
            changed = live.changed if live is not None else None
            over = live is None or live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES
            while True:
                try:
                    page = self.store.events_after(execution_id, after, EVENT_PAGE)
                except ValidationError as exc:
                    raise WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.INTERNAL, f"a stored event of {execution_id} is unreadable"
                    ) from exc
                for event in page:
                    yield event
                    after = event.seq
                    if isinstance(event, ResultEvent):
                        return
                if len(page) < EVENT_PAGE:
                    break
            if over or changed is None:
                return
            # Every reader shares the future: one that goes away must not cancel it.
            if heartbeat is None:
                await asyncio.shield(changed)
                continue
            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(changed), heartbeat)
            except TimeoutError:
                yield None

    async def wait(self, execution_id: str) -> Execution:
        """The execution once it is terminal."""
        while True:
            live = self._live.get(execution_id)
            if live is None:
                return self.get(execution_id)
            if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES:
                return live.execution
            # Every waiter shares the future: one that goes away must not cancel it.
            await asyncio.shield(live.changed)

    async def cancel(self, execution_id: str, project_id: str | None = None) -> Execution:
        execution = self.get(execution_id, project_id)
        live = self._live.get(execution_id)
        if live is None or live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES or live.final is not None:
            return execution
        already_requested = live.cancel_requested
        self.store.cancel_intent(execution_id)
        live.cancel_requested = True
        if live.dispatched and not already_requested:
            if execution.kind == "job" or (live.channel is not None and live.channel.daemon_token):
                live.cancel_watchdog = self._spawn(self._watch_cancel(live))
            try:
                await self._send_cancel(live)
            except WorkerError:
                if live.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
                    raise
        elif not live.dispatched:
            self._finish(
                live,
                ExecutionState.CANCELLED,
                Result(
                    error=ErrorInfo(kind=ErrorKind.CANCELLED, message="cancelled before it started")
                ),
            )
        return live.execution

    async def _watch_cancel(self, live: _Live) -> None:
        """A direct job cancel has its own deadline, independent of the wall-time limit."""
        await asyncio.sleep(CANCEL_GRACE)
        if live.execution.state in TERMINAL_STATES or live.final is not None:
            return
        channel = live.channel
        self._lose(live, "the executor that did not confirm job cancellation")
        if channel is not None:
            await channel.shutdown()

    async def _send_cancel(self, live: _Live) -> None:
        if live.execution.state not in (ExecutionState.CANCELLING, *TERMINAL_STATES):
            live.execution = live.execution.model_copy(update={"state": ExecutionState.CANCELLING})
            self._state(live, ExecutionState.CANCELLING)
            self.store.update_execution(live.execution)
        # Only the executor it was sent to has it; never start another one to cancel.
        channel = live.channel
        if channel is None or channel.closed:
            return
        await channel.request("cancel", execution=live.execution.execution_id)

    async def restart_kernel(self, request: KernelRestartRequest) -> KernelInfo:
        context = request.context
        self.package_admission(context.environment_id)
        async with self._using(context.environment_id) as channel:
            if not await self._sync_package_gate(context.environment_id, channel):
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "legacy executor cannot fence kernel restart"
                )
            self.package_admission(context.environment_id)
            reply = await channel.request(
                "restart", session=context.session_id, language=request.language, reply_timeout=180
            )
            kernel, _ = self._kernel(
                context.environment_id,
                context.session_id,
                reply.get("kernel"),
                True,
                project_id=context.project_id,
                restarted=True,
                expected_channel=channel,
            )
            if kernel is None:
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.INTERNAL, "the executor did not describe the kernel")
            return kernel

    async def close_session(self, request: SessionCloseRequest) -> SessionClosed:
        """Cancel and reap jobs, then stop kernels. Starts racing the close are refused."""
        context = request.context
        key = (context.project_id, context.environment_id, context.session_id)
        observer = self._kernel_observations.get(context.environment_id)
        if observer is not None and observer.scope == key:
            observer.valid = False  # close may finish before its old reply arrives
        self._closing_sessions[key] = self._closing_sessions.get(key, 0) + 1
        try:
            jobs = [
                job
                for job in self._running_jobs(context.environment_id)
                if job.context.project_id == context.project_id
                and job.context.session_id == context.session_id
            ]
            await self._cancel_jobs(jobs)
            return await self._close_session(request)
        finally:
            if self._closing_sessions[key] == 1:
                self._closing_sessions.pop(key)
            else:
                self._closing_sessions[key] -= 1

    async def _close_session(self, request: SessionCloseRequest) -> SessionClosed:
        context = request.context
        environment = self._environments.get(context.environment_id)
        channel = environment.channel if environment is not None else None
        if environment is None or channel is None or channel.closed:
            return SessionClosed()
        environment.requests += 1
        try:
            reply = await channel.request(
                "close_session", session=context.session_id, reply_timeout=180
            )
        finally:
            environment.requests -= 1
            environment.last_used = time.monotonic()
        raw: object = reply.get("kernels")
        stopped: list[KernelInfo] = []
        for item in cast(list[object], raw) if isinstance(raw, list) else []:
            kernel, _ = self._kernel(context.environment_id, context.session_id, item, False)
            if kernel is not None:
                stopped.append(kernel)
        return SessionClosed(kernels=tuple(stopped))

    async def capabilities(self, environment_id: str) -> Capabilities:
        environment = await self._environment(environment_id)
        if environment.location is None:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, f"environment {environment_id} has no executor"
            )
        return Capabilities(
            protocol=PROTOCOL_VERSION,
            languages=tuple(name for name in environment.languages if name in LANGUAGES),
            location=self._located(environment_id, environment) or environment.location,
            features=tuple(name for name in environment.features if name in FEATURES),
        )

    # Files. Replies are checked like events: a malformed one is an internal error.

    async def _read_range(
        self,
        channel: ExecutorChannel,
        request: ReadFileRequest,
        offset: int,
        length: int,
        *,
        hashed: bool,
    ) -> _Range:
        reply = await channel.request(
            "read",
            session=request.context.session_id,
            path=request.path,
            offset=offset,
            length=length,
            hash=hashed,
        )
        try:
            encoded = reply["content_b64"]
            if not isinstance(encoded, str):
                raise TypeError("content_b64")
            data = base64.b64decode(encoded, validate=True)
            size, start = _integer(reply.get("size"), 0, 2**62), _integer(reply.get("offset"), 0)
            sha256 = reply.get("sha256")
            if size is None or start != offset or len(data) > length or offset + len(data) > size:
                raise ValueError("a range that was not asked for")
            if hashed and not (isinstance(sha256, str) and len(sha256) == 64):
                raise ValueError("no SHA-256")
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:  # binascii.Error is a ValueError
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.INTERNAL, f"the executor sent a malformed file reply ({exc})"
            ) from exc
        return _Range(
            size=size,
            sha256=sha256 if hashed else None,
            modified=_epoch(reply.get("modified")),
            offset=offset,
            data=data,
            content_b64=encoded,
            eof=reply.get("eof") is True,
        )

    async def read_file(self, request: ReadFileRequest) -> FileContent:
        async with self._using(request.context.environment_id) as channel:
            await self._sync_shared(request.context, request.path, channel)
            found = await self._read_range(
                channel, request, request.offset, request.length, hashed=True
            )
            return _checked(
                FileContent,
                path=request.path,
                sha256=found.sha256,
                size=found.size,
                modified_at=found.modified,
                offset=found.offset,
                content_b64=found.content_b64,
                eof=found.eof,
            )

    async def write_file(self, request: WriteFileRequest) -> WriteFileResult:
        context = request.context
        async with self._using(context.environment_id) as channel:
            fields: dict[str, Any] = {
                "path": request.path,
                "content_b64": request.content_b64,
                "expected_sha256": request.expected_sha256,
                "create_only": request.create_only,
            }
            if self.shared is not None and _in_shared(request.path):
                # The expected SHA-256 is checked against the project's version (D79).
                notices: list[str] = []
                try:
                    reply = await self.shared.write(
                        context.project_id,
                        context.environment_id,
                        context.session_id,
                        channel,
                        fields,
                        SHARED_TIMEOUT,
                        notices,
                    )
                finally:  # what the sync found is told even when the write is refused
                    self._tell(context, notices)
            else:
                reply = await channel.request("write", session=context.session_id, **fields)
            return _checked(WriteFileResult, sha256=reply.get("sha256"), size=reply.get("size"))

    async def list_files(self, request: ListFilesRequest) -> FileListing:
        context = request.context
        async with self._using(context.environment_id) as channel:
            await self._sync_shared(context, request.path, channel)
            reply = await channel.request("list", session=context.session_id, path=request.path)
            raw = reply.get("entries")
            every = cast(list[object], raw) if isinstance(raw, list) else []
            entries = every[:MAX_LIST]
            listed: list[FileEntry] = []
            for entry in entries:
                item = cast(dict[str, Any], entry) if isinstance(entry, dict) else {}
                listed.append(
                    _checked(
                        FileEntry,
                        name=item.get("name"),
                        type=item.get("type"),
                        size=item.get("size"),
                        modified_at=_epoch(item.get("modified")),
                    )
                )
            return FileListing(
                path=request.path,
                entries=tuple(listed),
                truncated=reply.get("truncated") is True or len(entries) < len(every),
            )

    async def _blob_io(self, function: Callable[..., Any], *args: object) -> Any:
        """Keep the actual thread owned before cancellation can close/reuse its FD."""
        future = asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
            self._blob_pool, partial(function, *args)
        )
        result, cancelled = await capture.owned(future)
        if cancelled:
            raise asyncio.CancelledError
        return result

    async def _capture_range(
        self,
        channel: ExecutorChannel,
        reading: ReadFileRequest,
        offset: int,
        deadline: float,
        owner: _Publication,
        *,
        hashed: bool,
    ) -> _Range:
        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if remaining <= 0:
            raise TimeoutError
        capture_id = new_id("cap")
        try:
            owner.lease = self.store.dispatch_capture(
                owner.lease,
                channel.incarnation,
                capture_id,
                self.store.capture_binding(reading.context.environment_id, channel.incarnation)
                if channel.daemon_token is not None
                else None,
            )
        except ValueError as exc:
            owner.certain = False
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, str(exc)) from exc
        owner.certain = False
        # Keep the request pending so cancellation waits for the original reader as
        # well as the explicit cleanup acknowledgement. A mere HTTP timeout cannot
        # cancel a filesystem operation in the sandbox.
        task = asyncio.create_task(
            channel.request(
                "capture_read",
                capture_id=capture_id,
                session=reading.context.session_id,
                path=reading.path,
                offset=offset,
                length=MAX_READ_BYTES,
                max_bytes=min(capture.MAX_BYTES, self.max_artifact_size),
                hash=hashed,
                timeout=remaining,
                reply_timeout=None,
            )
        )
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(remaining):
                reply = await asyncio.shield(task)
            if reply.get("capture_id") != capture_id or reply.get("cleaned") is not True:
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.INTERNAL, "capture reply lacks exact cleanup proof")
            owner.certain = True
        except BaseException:

            async def cleanup() -> None:
                try:
                    async with asyncio.timeout(1):
                        cancelled = await channel.request(
                            "capture_cancel", capture_id=capture_id, reply_timeout=1
                        )
                    if (
                        cancelled.get("capture_id") == capture_id
                        and cancelled.get("cleaned") is True
                    ):
                        owner.certain = True
                finally:
                    # This task only owns a protocol reply, not guest filesystem
                    # work. No ACK means its durable lease stays held; the guest
                    # pool still owns the actual helper until observed exit.
                    if not task.done():
                        task.cancel()
                    await asyncio.gather(task, return_exceptions=True)
                    if not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is None:
                        result = task.result()
                        if result.get("capture_id") == capture_id and result.get("cleaned") is True:
                            owner.certain = True

            with contextlib.suppress(WorkerError, TimeoutError):
                await capture.owned(asyncio.create_task(cleanup()))
            if not owner.certain:
                raise WorkerError(
                    ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE,
                    "capture cleanup outcome is unknown; durable admission remains held",
                ) from None
            raise
        error: object = reply.get("capture_error")
        if error is not None:
            record = cast(dict[str, Any], error) if isinstance(error, dict) else {}
            kind, message = record.get("kind"), record.get("message")
            if (
                not isinstance(kind, str)
                or len(kind) > 32
                or not isinstance(message, str)
                or len(message) > 512
            ):
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.INTERNAL, "invalid capture failure metadata")
            try:
                error_kind = ErrorKind(kind)
            except ValueError:
                error_kind = ErrorKind.INTERNAL
            raise WorkerError(error_kind, message)
        try:
            encoded = reply.get("content_b64")
            if not isinstance(encoded, str) or len(encoded) > 4 * ((MAX_READ_BYTES + 2) // 3):
                raise ValueError("range encoding exceeds its bound")
            data = base64.b64decode(encoded, validate=True)
            limit = min(capture.MAX_BYTES, self.max_artifact_size)
            size = _integer(reply.get("size"), 0, limit)
            start = _integer(reply.get("offset"), 0, capture.MAX_BYTES)
            sha256, stamp = reply.get("sha256"), reply.get("stamp")
            eof = reply.get("eof")
            modified = reply.get("modified")
            if (
                size is None
                or start != offset
                or len(data) > MAX_READ_BYTES
                or offset + len(data) > size
                or type(eof) is not bool
                or eof != (offset + len(data) == size)
                or not isinstance(stamp, str)
                or re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", stamp) is None
                or (
                    hashed
                    and (
                        not isinstance(sha256, str) or re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", sha256) is None
                    )
                )
                or (not hashed and sha256 is not None)
                or not isinstance(modified, int | float)
                or isinstance(modified, bool)
                or not math.isfinite(modified)
            ):
                raise ValueError("invalid capture metadata")
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise WorkerError(
                ErrorKind.INTERNAL, "the executor sent a malformed capture reply"
            ) from exc
        return _Range(size, sha256, _epoch(modified), offset, data, encoded, eof, stamp)

    def _capture_usage(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        try:
            for lease in self.store.capture_leases():
                counts[lease.environment_id] = counts.get(lease.environment_id, 0) + 1
        except ValueError:
            return {"unknown-corrupt-state": 4}
        return counts

    async def _reconcile_captures(self, environment_id: str, channel: ExecutorChannel) -> None:
        """Only held host-drained leases can receive same-incarnation cleanup ACKs.

        Active rows left by an abruptly lost worker remain conservative holds:
        another process may still own host I/O. Neither time nor a new executor
        incarnation proves that ownership ended.
        """
        protocol = channel.hello.get("artifact_capture_protocol")
        if type(protocol) is not int or protocol != capture.PROTOCOL:
            return
        try:
            leases = self.store.capture_leases()
        except ValueError:
            return
        for lease in leases:
            if (
                lease.phase != "held"
                or lease.environment_id != environment_id
                or lease.incarnation != channel.incarnation
                or not lease.capture_id
            ):
                continue
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(1):
                    reply = await channel.request("capture_cancel", capture_id=lease.capture_id)
                if reply.get("capture_id") == lease.capture_id and reply.get("cleaned") is True:
                    self.store.acknowledge_capture(lease)
            except (WorkerError, TimeoutError, ValueError):
                _log.warning("capture cleanup remains unknown; durable admission held")
        self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()

    async def publish(self, request: PublishRequest) -> ArtifactRef:
        """Admit four durable publications, two per environment, without queued work.

        Unknown guest cleanup holds admission even after actual host work drains;
        this is a byte observation, never proof of writer closure.
        """
        environment_id = request.context.environment_id
        if self._closing or environment_id in self._released_environments:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, "artifact capture admission limit reached")
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.capture_timeout
        try:
            lease = self.store.reserve_capture(new_id("pub"), environment_id)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.UNAVAILABLE, str(exc)) from exc
        owner = _Publication(lease)
        task = asyncio.create_task(self._publish(request, deadline, owner))
        self._captures.add(task)
        self._capture_owners[task] = owner
        self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()

        def finished(done: asyncio.Task[ArtifactRef]) -> None:
            self._captures.discard(done)
            self._capture_owners.pop(done)
            try:
                self.store.finish_capture(owner.lease, certain=owner.certain)
            except ValueError:
                _log.error("capture completion cannot release displaced admission; held")
            self._capture_counts = self._capture_usage()
            if not done.cancelled():
                done.exception()

        task.add_done_callback(finished)
        try:
            return await asyncio.shield(task)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            task.cancel()
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await capture.owned(task)
            raise

    async def _publish(
        self, request: PublishRequest, deadline: float, owner: _Publication
    ) -> ArtifactRef:
        context = request.context
        writer: BlobWriter | None = None
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout_at(
                asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + max(0, deadline - time.monotonic())
            ):
                async with self._using(context.environment_id) as channel:
                    protocol = channel.hello.get("artifact_capture_protocol")
                    if type(protocol) is not int or protocol != capture.PROTOCOL:
                        raise WorkerError(
                            ErrorKind.UNSUPPORTED,
                            "this executor lacks bounded artifact capture protocol 1",
                        )
                    reading = ReadFileRequest(context=context, path=request.path)
                    changed = WorkerError(
                        ErrorKind.CONFLICT, f"{request.path} changed while it was published"
                    )
                    creating = asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
                        self._blob_pool, self.blobs.writer
                    )
                    writer, cancelled = await capture.owned(creating)
                    if cancelled:
                        raise asyncio.CancelledError
                    found = await self._capture_range(
                        channel, reading, 0, deadline, owner, hashed=True
                    )
                    size, sha256, stamp = found.size, found.sha256, found.stamp
                    offset = 0
                    while True:
                        await self._blob_io(writer.write, found.data)
                        offset += len(found.data)
                        if offset == size:
                            break
                        if len(found.data) < MAX_READ_BYTES or found.eof:
                            raise changed
                        found = await self._capture_range(
                            channel, reading, offset, deadline, owner, hashed=False
                        )
                        if found.size != size or found.stamp != stamp:
                            raise changed
                    if (
                        sha256 is None
                        or writer.size != size
                        or not await self._blob_io(writer.commit, sha256)
                    ):
                        raise changed
                    media_type = (
                        request.media_type
                        or mimetypes.guess_type(request.path)[0]
                        or "application/octet-stream"
                    )
                    produced_by = await self._blob_io(
                        self.store.producer_hint,
                        context.project_id,
                        context.environment_id,
                        context.session_id,
                        request.path,
                        deadline,
                    )
                    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                        raise TimeoutError
                    artifact = ArtifactRef(
                        artifact_id=new_id("art"),
                        project_id=context.project_id,
                        sha256=sha256,
                        size=size,
                        media_type=media_type,
                        source_path=request.path,
                        produced_by=produced_by,
                        created_at=_now(),
                    )
                    self.store.insert_artifact(artifact)
                    return artifact
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            raise WorkerError(
